title.en: Volume 47 Biographies 7: Liu Huaisu, Meng Huaiyu, Liu Jingxuan, Tan Zhi
title.raw: 卷四十七 列傳第七 劉懷肅 孟懷玉 劉敬宣 檀祗 Volume 47 Biographies 7: Liu Huaisu, Meng Huaiyu, Liu Jingxuan, Tan Zhi

sentences.zh: 列傳第七 劉懷肅 孟懷玉

translations.literal: Biographies 7: Liu Huaisu, Meng Huaiyu
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 7: Liu Huaisu and Meng Huaiyu

sentences.zh: 〈弟龍符〉

translations.literal: 〈Younger brother Longfu〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Younger brother Longfu〉

sentences.zh: 劉敬宣 檀祗

translations.literal: Liu Jingxuan, Tan Zhi
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jingxuan and Tan Zhi

sentences.zh: 劉懷肅，彭城人，高祖從母兄也。

translations.literal: Liu Huaisu was a man of Pengcheng and was the elder son of the Gaozu's mother's sister.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Huaisu, a native of Pengcheng, was a cousin on Emperor Wu's mother's side.

sentences.zh: 家世貧窶，而躬耕好學。

translations.literal: His family had long been poor, yet he personally plowed the fields and loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long been destitute, yet he worked his own fields and loved learning.

sentences.zh: 初為劉敬宣寧朔府司馬，東征孫恩，有戰功，又為龍驤司馬、費令。

translations.literal: At first he served as Ningshuo-fu Major under Liu Jingxuan; in the eastern campaign against Sun En he won military merit, and later became Longxiang Major and magistrate of Fei.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as major of Liu Jingxuan's Ningshuo headquarters; in the eastern campaign against Sun En he distinguished himself in battle, and was later made major of the Longxiang command and magistrate of Fei.

sentences.zh: 聞高祖起義，棄縣來奔。

translations.literal: When he heard that the Gaozu had raised his army, he abandoned his county post and came to join him.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that Emperor Wu had risen in arms, he abandoned his county post and rushed to join him.

sentences.zh: 京邑平定，振武將軍道規追桓玄，以懷肅為司馬。

translations.literal: After the capital region was pacified, Zhenwu General Daogui pursued Huan Xuan and made Huaisu his major.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was pacified, Zhenwu General Liu Daogui pursued Huan Xuan and appointed Huaisu his major.

sentences.zh: 玄留何澹之、郭銓等戍桑落洲，進擊破之。

translations.literal: Xuan left He Danzhi, Guo Quan, and others to garrison Sangluo Isle; advancing, they defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan had left He Danzhi, Guo Quan, and others to hold Sangluo Isle; Huaisu advanced and routed them.

sentences.zh: 潁川太守劉統平，除高平太守。

translations.literal: When Yingchuan Administrator Liu Tong was pacified, he was appointed Administrator of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: After Yingchuan Administrator Liu Tong was subdued, he was appointed administrator of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 玄既死，從子振大破義軍於楊林，義軍退尋陽。

translations.literal: After Xuan had died, his nephew Zhen inflicted a great defeat on the righteous army at Yanglin, and the righteous army withdrew to Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Huan Xuan's death, his nephew Zhen routed the loyalist army at Yanglin, forcing it to fall back to Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 懷肅與江夏相張暢之攻澹之於西塞，破之。

translations.literal: Huaisu, together with Zhang Changzhi, Chancellor of Jiangxia, attacked Danzhi at Xisai and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Huaisu joined Zhang Changzhi, chancellor of Jiangxia, in attacking Danzhi at Xisai and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 偽鎮東將軍馮該戍夏口東岸，孟山圖據魯山城，桓仙客守偃月壘，皆連壁相望。

translations.literal: The false General Who Pacifies the East Feng Gai garrisoned the eastern bank of Xiakou; Meng Shantu held Lushan Fortress, and Huan Xianke guarded Yanyue Rampart; all linked their walls and faced one another.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel General Who Pacifies the East Feng Gai held the east bank of Xiakou; Meng Shantu occupied Lushan Fortress and Huan Xianke held Yanyue Rampart, their fortifications linked in a continuous line.

sentences.zh: 懷肅與道規攻之，躬擐甲胄，陷二城，馮該走石城，生擒仙客。

translations.literal: Huaisu and Daogui attacked them; donning armor himself, he took two cities; Feng Gai fled to Shicheng, and Xianke was captured alive.
translations.idiomatic: Huaisu and Daogui attacked them; Huaisu donned armor himself, stormed two cities, drove Feng Gai to Shicheng, and took Xianke alive.

sentences.zh: 義熙元年正月，振敗走，道規遣懷肅平石城，斬馮該及其子山靖。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Yixi, Zhen was defeated and fled; Daogui sent Huaisu to pacify Shicheng and beheaded Feng Gai and his son Shanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Yixi 1, Zhen was defeated and fled; Daogui sent Huaisu to take Shicheng and executed Feng Gai and his son Shanjing.

sentences.zh: 三月，桓振復襲江陵，荊州刺史司馬休之出奔，懷肅自雲杜馳赴，日夜兼行，七日而至。

translations.literal: In the third month, Huan Zhen again raided Jiangling; Jingzhou Inspector Sima Xiuzhi fled; Huaisu galloped from Yundu, traveling day and night without rest, and arrived in seven days.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Huan Zhen struck Jiangling again; Jingzhou inspector Sima Xiuzhi fled; Huaisu raced from Yundu day and night without pause and arrived in seven days.

sentences.zh: 振勒兵三萬，旗幟蔽野，躍馬橫矛，躬自突陳。

translations.literal: Zhen marshaled thirty thousand troops; banners and flags covered the fields; leaping his horse and leveling his spear, he personally charged the battle line.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen mustered thirty thousand men; banners blotted out the plain; spurring his horse with spear leveled, he charged the line himself.

sentences.zh: 流矢傷懷肅額，眾懼欲奔，懷肅瞋目奮戰，士氣益壯。

translations.literal: A stray arrow wounded Huaisu's forehead; the troops feared and wished to flee; Huaisu glared and fought fiercely, and the army's morale grew stronger.
translations.idiomatic: A stray arrow struck Huaisu in the forehead; his men panicked and nearly broke; glaring, he fought on fiercely, and their spirit surged anew.

sentences.zh: 於是士卒爭先，臨陣斬振首。

translations.literal: Thereupon the soldiers vied to be first; on the field they beheaded Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers then rushed forward and cut off Zhen's head on the battlefield.

sentences.zh: 江陵既平，休之反鎮，執懷肅手曰：「微子之力，吾無所歸矣。

translations.literal: After Jiangling was pacified, Xiuzhi returned to his post, took Huaisu's hand, and said: "But for your strength, I would have nowhere to turn.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jiangling was secure, Xiuzhi returned to his post, took Huaisu's hand, and said, "Without your help, I would have had nowhere to go.

sentences.zh: 」偽輔國將軍符嗣、馬孫、偽龍驤將軍金符青、樂志等屯結江夏，懷肅又討之，梟樂志等。

translations.literal: " The false General Who Assists the State Fu Si, Ma Sun, the false Longxiang General Jin Fuqing, Yue Zhi, and others massed at Jiangxia; Huaisu again campaigned against them and exposed the heads of Yue Zhi and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: " The rebel Generals Who Assist the State Fu Si and Ma Sun, the rebel Longxiang General Jin Fuqing, Yue Zhi, and others had gathered at Jiangxia; Huaisu campaigned against them again and displayed the heads of Yue Zhi and his fellows.

sentences.zh: 道規加懷肅督江夏九郡，權鎮夏口。

translations.literal: Daogui further appointed Huaisu to oversee the nine commanderies of Jiangxia and to hold Xiaokou on an acting basis.
translations.idiomatic: Daogui further put Huaisu in charge of the nine Jiangxia commanderies and gave him acting authority at Xiaokou.

sentences.zh: 除通直郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Tongzhi Lang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed gentleman for direct communication.

sentences.zh: 仍為輔國將軍、淮南、歷陽二郡太守。

translations.literal: He was then made General Who Assists the State and Administrator of the two commanderies Huainan and Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made General Who Assists the State and administrator of Huainan and Liyang.

sentences.zh: 二年，又領劉毅撫軍司馬，軍、郡如故。

translations.literal: In the second year he also took charge as Fuying Major under Liu Yi; his military and commandery posts remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he also served as major on Liu Yi's staff; his military and prefectural posts were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 以義功封東興縣侯，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: For merit in the righteous cause he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dongxing County with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: For his service in the founding cause he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dongxing with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 其冬，桓石綏、司馬國璠、陳襲於胡桃山聚眾為寇，懷肅率步騎討破之。

translations.literal: That winter, Huan Shisui, Sima Guofan, and Chen Xi gathered a host at Hutao Mountain and raided as bandits; Huaisu led infantry and cavalry to campaign against them and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Huan Shisui, Sima Guofan, and Chen Xi raised a band at Hutao Mountain; Huaisu led foot and horse against them and broke them.

sentences.zh: 江淮間群蠻及桓氏餘黨為亂，自請出討，既行失旨，毅上表免懷肅官。

translations.literal: Tribal groups between the Jiang and Huai and the remaining partisans of the Huan clan rose in disorder; he volunteered to go out and suppress them, but once he had set out he lost imperial favor, and Yi memorialized to strip Huaisu of his offices.
translations.idiomatic: Tribal groups along the Jiang and Huai and Huan loyalists were in revolt; he asked to lead a campaign, but once underway he fell from favor, and Liu Yi memorialized to strip him of office.

sentences.zh: 三年，卒，時年四十一。

translations.literal: In the third year he died, aged forty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he died, at the age of forty-one.

sentences.zh: 追贈左將軍。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given the Left General.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Left General.

sentences.zh: 無子，弟懷慎以子蔚祖嗣封，官至江夏內史。

translations.literal: He had no son; his younger brother Huaishen had his son Weizu succeed to the enfeoffment, and he reached the post of Interior Governor of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son; his younger brother Huaishen had his son Weizu inherit the title, and Weizu rose to interior governor of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 蔚祖卒，子道存嗣。

translations.literal: Weizu died, and his son Daocun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Weizu died, his son Daocun inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 太祖元嘉末，為太尉江夏王義恭諮議參軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanjia under the Taizu, he served as Staff Adviser to the Grand Marshal, Prince of Jiangxia Yigong.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuanjia era under Emperor Wen, he served as staff adviser to Grand Marshal Liu Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 世祖伐元兇，義軍至新亭，道存出奔，元兇殺其母以徇。

translations.literal: When the Shizu campaigned against the usurper, the righteous army reached Xinting; Daocun fled; the usurper killed his mother and displayed her body as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu marched against the usurper, the loyalist army reached Xinting; Daocun fled, and the usurper killed his mother and exposed her corpse as a warning.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝景和中，為義恭太宰從事中郎。

translations.literal: Under the Deposed Former Emperor in the Jinghe era, he was Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat on the staff of Yigong as Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Qianfei in the Jinghe era, he was attendant gentleman on Liu Yigong's staff as grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 義恭敗，以黨與下獄死。

translations.literal: When Yigong was defeated, as a partisan he was cast into prison and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Yigong fell, he was imprisoned as a partisan and died there.

sentences.zh: 懷肅次弟懷敬，澀訥無才能。

translations.literal: Huaisu's next younger brother Huaaijing was dull and tongue-tied and without ability.
translations.idiomatic: Huaisu's next younger brother, Huaijing, was slow-spoken and without talent.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖產而皇妣殂，孝皇帝貧薄，無由得乳人，議欲不舉高祖。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when the Gaozu was born the imperial mother died; the Xiaohuangdi was poor and had no means to obtain a wet nurse, and they discussed not raising the Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu was born, his mother died; his father was too poor to hire a wet nurse, and the family even considered abandoning the infant.

sentences.zh: 高祖從母生懷敬，未朞，乃斷懷敬乳，而自養高祖。

translations.literal: The Gaozu's mother's sister had borne Huaijing; before the first birthday they weaned Huaijing and herself nursed the Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu's aunt had just borne Huaijing; before the child was a year old she weaned him and nursed Emperor Wu herself.

sentences.zh: 高祖以舊恩，懷敬累見寵授，至會稽太守，尚書，金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Because of this old kindness, the Gaozu repeatedly favored Huaijing with appointments, up to Administrator of Kuaiji, Minister, and Grand Master for the Palace with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: Out of gratitude for that old debt, Emperor Wu repeatedly favored Huaijing with office, raising him to Kuaiji administrator, minister, and grand master for the palace with golden seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 懷敬子真道，為錢唐令。

translations.literal: Huaijing's son Zhendao was magistrate of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Huaijing's son Zhendao served as magistrate of Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十三年，東土饑，上遣揚州治中從事史沈演之巡行在所，演之上表曰：「宰邑輔政，必其簡惠成能；

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yuanjia, the eastern regions suffered famine; the emperor sent Yangzhou Attendant Clerk Shen Yanzhi to tour the affected districts; Yanzhi memorialized: "To govern a district and assist in administration, one must be selected for simplicity and kindness to succeed;
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 13 the eastern provinces suffered famine; the court sent Yangzhou attendant clerk Shen Yanzhi to inspect the stricken districts. Yanzhi memorialized, "To govern a district and aid the administration, a man must be chosen for simplicity and kindness if he is to succeed;

sentences.zh: 蒞職闡治，務以利民著績。

translations.literal: when one takes office and expounds good government, the task is to benefit the people and win a record of achievement.
translations.idiomatic: when he takes office and carries out good government, his aim must be to benefit the people and leave a record of achievement.

sentences.zh: 故王奐見紀於前，叔卿流稱於後。

translations.literal: Thus Wang Huan was recorded in praise in earlier times, and Shuqing won flowing renown afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huan was praised in earlier times, and Shuqing won lasting renown afterward.

sentences.zh: 竊見錢唐令劉真道、餘杭令劉道錫，皆奉公恤民，恪勤匪懈，百姓稱詠，訟訴希簡。

translations.literal: I have observed that Qiantang Magistrate Liu Zhendao and Yuhang Magistrate Liu Daoxi both serve the public and show compassion to the people, diligent and unwearying; the common people sing their praise, and lawsuits are few and simple.
translations.idiomatic: I have observed that Qiantang magistrate Liu Zhendao and Yuhang magistrate Liu Daoxi both serve the public faithfully and care for the people, diligent and tireless; the people praise them, and lawsuits are few.

sentences.zh: 又翦蕩凶非，屢能擒獲。

translations.literal: They have also cut down violent wrongdoers and repeatedly captured them.
translations.idiomatic: They have also rooted out violent criminals and repeatedly captured them.

sentences.zh: 災水之初，餘杭高堤崩潰，洪流迅激，勢不可量；

translations.literal: At the beginning of the flood disaster, Yuhang's high dike collapsed; the torrent was swift and violent, its force beyond reckoning;
translations.idiomatic: At the onset of the floods, Yuhang's high dike burst; the torrent was swift and violent beyond measure;

sentences.zh: 道錫躬先吏民，親執板築，塘既還立，縣邑獲全。

translations.literal: Daoxi took the lead before officials and people, personally wielding the tamping boards; once the embankment was restored, the county seat was preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: Daoxi led officials and people alike, personally working the tamping boards; once the dike was rebuilt, the county was saved.

sentences.zh: 經歷諸縣，訪核名實，並為二邦之首最，治民之良宰。

translations.literal: Having toured the various counties and verified names against facts, both stand foremost among the two prefectures as excellent magistrates who govern the people well.
translations.idiomatic: Having toured the counties and verified their records, I find both the foremost magistrates of their two prefectures—exemplary rulers of the people.

sentences.zh: 」上嘉之，各賜穀千斛，以真道為步兵校尉。

translations.literal: " The emperor praised them and granted each a thousand hu of grain; Zhendao was made Commandant of Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor commended them and granted each a thousand hu of grain; Zhendao was made commandant of footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 十四年，出為梁、南秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he went out as Inspector of the two provinces Liang and Nanqin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was sent out as inspector of Liang and Nanqin.

sentences.zh: 十八年，氐賊楊難當侵寇漢中，真道率軍討破之。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the Di bandit Yang Dandang invaded and raided Hanzhong; Zhendao led troops to campaign against him and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year the Di chieftain Yang Dandang invaded Hanzhong; Zhendao led an army against him and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 而難當寇盜猶不已，太祖遣龍驤將軍裴方明率禁兵五千，受真道節度。

translations.literal: Yet Dandang's raids did not cease; the Taizu sent Longxiang General Pei Fangming with five thousand palace troops to accept Zhendao's command.
translations.idiomatic: But Dandang's raids continued; Emperor Wen sent Longxiang General Pei Fangming with five thousand palace troops under Zhendao's command.

sentences.zh: 十九年，方明至武興，率太子積弩將軍劉康祖、後軍參軍梁坦、陳彌、裴肅之、安西參軍段叔文、魯尚期、始興王國常侍劉僧秀、綏遠將軍馬洗、振武將軍王奐之等，進次潭谷，去臯蘭數里。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Fangming reached Wuxing and led the Heir Apparent's General of Repeated Crossbows Liu Kangzu, Rear Army Staff Officer Liang Tan, Chen Mi, Pei Suzhi, Anxi Staff Officer Duan Shuwen, Lu Shangqi, Regular Attendant of the Principality of Shixing Liu Sengxiu, General Who Pacifies the Distance Ma Xi, Zhenwu General Wang Huazhi, and others; advancing they halted at Tangu, several li from Gaolan.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year Fangming reached Wuxing and advanced with Heir Apparent's general of repeated crossbows Liu Kangzu, rear army staff officer Liang Tan, Chen Mi, Pei Suzhi, Anxi staff officer Duan Shuwen, Lu Shangqi, regular attendant of the Principality of Shixing Liu Sengxiu, general who pacifies the distance Ma Xi, Zhenwu general Wang Huazhi, and others to Tangu, a few li from Gaolan.

sentences.zh: 難當遣其建節將軍苻弘祖、啖元等固守蘭皋，鎮北將軍苻德義於外為游軍，難當子撫軍大將軍和重兵繼其後。

translations.literal: Dandang sent his General Who Establishes the Staff Fu Hongzu, Tan Yuan, and others to hold fast at Langao; General Who Pacifies the North Fu Deyi served outside as a mobile force; Dandang's son, General-in-Chief Who Pacifies the Army He, followed with heavy troops.
translations.idiomatic: Dandang sent his general who establishes the staff Fu Hongzu and Tan Yuan to hold Langao, his general who pacifies the north Fu Deyi to serve as a mobile force outside, and his son He, general-in-chief who pacifies the army, to follow with a large rear guard.

sentences.zh: 方明進擊，大破之於濁水，斬弘祖并三千餘級。

translations.literal: Fangming advanced to attack and inflicted a great defeat on them at Zhuoshui, beheading Hongzu together with more than three thousand of the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Fangming attacked and routed them at Zhuoshui, killing Hongzu and more than three thousand of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 遣康祖追之，過臯蘭二千餘里。

translations.literal: He sent Kangzu in pursuit, passing more than two thousand li beyond Gaolan.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Kangzu in pursuit more than two thousand li beyond Gaolan.

sentences.zh: 和又遣德義助戰，康祖又大破之，和退保脩城。

translations.literal: He again sent Deyi to assist in the fighting; Kangzu again inflicted a great defeat; He withdrew to hold Xiucheng.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Deyi to reinforce the fight; Kangzu routed them again, and He fell back to Xiucheng.

sentences.zh: 難當遣建忠將軍楊林、振威將軍姚憲領二千騎就和，方明又率諸將攻之。

translations.literal: Dandang sent General Who Establishes Loyalty Yang Lin and General Who Shakes Might Yao Xian leading two thousand horsemen to join He; Fangming again led the generals to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Dandang sent general who establishes loyalty Yang Lin and general who shakes might Yao Xian with two thousand horsemen to join He; Fangming led the generals against them again.

sentences.zh: 和敗走，追至赤亭，難當席卷奔叛。

translations.literal: He was defeated and fled; they pursued to Chiting; Dandang swept up his belongings and fled in revolt.
translations.idiomatic: He was defeated and fled; the pursuit reached Chiting; Dandang gathered what he could and fled in disorder.

sentences.zh: 方明遣康祖直趣百頃，偽丞相楊萬壽等一時歸降。

translations.literal: Fangming sent Kangzu straight to Baiyu; the false Chancellor Yang Wanshou and others all surrendered at once.
translations.idiomatic: Fangming sent Kangzu straight to Baiyu; the rebel chancellor Yang Wanshou and others surrendered at once.

sentences.zh: 難當第三息虎先戍陰平，難當既走，虎逃竄民間，生禽之，送京都，斬於建康市。

translations.literal: Dandang's third son Hu had first garrisoned Yinping; once Dandang had fled, Hu hid among the common people; he was captured alive, sent to the capital, and beheaded in the market of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Dandang's third son Hu had garrisoned Yinping; when Dandang fled, Hu hid among the people, was taken alive, sent to the capital, and executed in the Jiankang market.

sentences.zh: 秦州刺史胡崇之西鎮百頃，行至濁水，為索虜所邀擊，敗沒。

translations.literal: Qinzhou Inspector Hu Chongzhi went west to garrison Baiyu; when he reached Zhuoshui he was intercepted and struck by the Suolu barbarians and was defeated and lost.
translations.idiomatic: Qinzhou inspector Hu Chongzhi marched west to garrison Baiyu; at Zhuoshui he was ambushed by the northern barbarians, defeated, and killed.

sentences.zh: 以真道為建威將軍、雍州刺史，方明輔國將軍、梁、南秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhendao was made General Who Establishes Might and Inspector of Yongzhou; Fangming was made General Who Assists the State and Inspector of the two provinces Liang and Nanqin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhendao was made general who establishes might and inspector of Yongzhou; Fangming was made general who assists the state and inspector of Liang and Nanqin.

sentences.zh: 方明辭不拜。

translations.literal: Fangming declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Fangming declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「往年氐豎楊難當造為叛亂，俛首者眾。

translations.literal: An edict said: "In former years the Di rebel Yang Dandang raised rebellion; many bowed their heads in submission.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "In former years the Di rebel Yang Dandang rose in rebellion; many submitted.

sentences.zh: 其長史楊萬壽、建節將軍姚憲，情不違順，屢進矢言。

translations.literal: His Chief Clerk Yang Wanshou and General Who Establishes the Staff Yao Xian, in sentiment not disobedient, repeatedly offered forthright counsel.
translations.idiomatic: His chief clerk Yang Wanshou and general who establishes the staff Yao Xian remained loyal in spirit and repeatedly offered honest counsel.

sentences.zh: 及凶醜宵遁，闔境崩擾，建忠將軍呂訓衛倉儲以候王師。

translations.literal: When the wicked villain fled by night, the whole region collapsed in turmoil; General Who Establishes Loyalty Lü Xun guarded the granaries to await the royal army.
translations.idiomatic: When the villain fled by night and the whole region fell into chaos, general who establishes loyalty Lü Xun guarded the granaries to await the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 寧朔將軍姜檀果烈懇到，志在宣力，濁水之捷，厥庸顯然，近者協贊義奮，乃心無替。

translations.literal: Ningshuo General Jiang Tan was resolute and earnest in loyalty, his will set on displaying his strength; at the victory at Zhuoshui his merit was plainly evident; recently he has aided the righteous cause with ardor, his heart unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Ningshuo general Jiang Tan was resolute and loyal, eager to serve; his merit at Zhuoshui was plain, and lately he has aided the campaign with undiminished zeal.

sentences.zh: 略陽苻昭，誠係本朝，亦同斯舉，俘擒偽將，獨克武興，推鋒致效，隕命寇手。

translations.literal: Fuzhao of Lueyang was sincerely bound to the dynasty and likewise joined this effort; capturing the false general, he alone took Wuxing; pressing the vanguard he achieved merit and lost his life to the enemy's hand.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhao of Lueyang was sincerely loyal to the dynasty and joined the effort; he captured a rebel general, took Wuxing alone, led the vanguard to victory, and fell to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 並事著屯險，感於予懷，宜蒙旌敘，榮慰存亡。

translations.literal: All their deeds were marked in perilous garrisons; moved in my breast, they should receive commendation and posthumous honors to comfort the living and the dead.
translations.idiomatic: All distinguished themselves in perilous posts; moved by their service, they should receive honors to comfort the living and the dead.

sentences.zh: 可贈萬壽龍驤將軍，昭武都太守；

translations.literal: Wanshou may be posthumously given Longxiang General and Administrator of Zhaowu Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Wanshou shall be posthumously made Longxiang general and administrator of Zhaowu commandery;

sentences.zh: 憲補員外散騎侍郎，訓駙馬都尉、奉朝請；

translations.literal: Xian may be appointed Supplementary Attendant Cavalier at Large; Xun may be made Commandant of the Horse Guards for the Imperial Son-in-Law and Court Attendant;
translations.idiomatic: Xian shall be appointed supplementary attendant cavalier at large; Xun shall be made commandant of the horse guards for the imperial son-in-law and court attendant;

sentences.zh: 檀征西大將軍司馬、仇池太守，宜並內徙。

translations.literal: Tan may be made Major on the staff of the General-in-Chief Who Conquers the West and Administrator of Chouci; all should be moved inward.
translations.idiomatic: Tan shall be made major on the staff of the general-in-chief who conquers the west and administrator of Chouci; all should be relocated inland.

sentences.zh: 可符雍、梁二州，厚加贍恤。

translations.literal: Orders may be sent to the two provinces Yong and Liang to grant generous support and relief.
translations.idiomatic: Orders shall go to Yong and Liang to provide generous support and relief.

sentences.zh: 」呂訓，略氐人呂先子也。

translations.literal: " Lü Xun was the son of Lü Xian, a man of the Lue Di.
translations.idiomatic: " Lü Xun was the son of Lü Xian of the Lue Di.

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「故晉壽太守姜道盛，前討仇池，志輸誠力，即戎著效，臨財能清。

translations.literal: Another edict said: "The late Jinshou Administrator Jiang Daosheng, in the former campaign against Chouci, devoted his will and strength in loyalty; taking the field he achieved merit; facing wealth he could remain pure.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict said, "The late Jinshou administrator Jiang Daosheng, in the campaign against Chouci, gave his loyalty and strength; in battle he distinguished himself and remained incorruptible before wealth.

sentences.zh: 近先登濁水，殞身鋒鏑，誠節俱亮，矜悼於懷。

translations.literal: Recently he was first to ascend at Zhuoshui and lost his life to blades and arrows; loyalty and integrity alike shine; I grieve and mourn him in my breast.
translations.idiomatic: Lately he led the assault at Zhuoshui and fell to the enemy's blades; his loyalty and integrity alike shine clear, and I mourn him deeply.

sentences.zh: 可贈給事中，賜錢千萬。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously given Palace Attendant and granted ten million in cash.
translations.idiomatic: He shall be posthumously made palace attendant and granted ten million in cash.

sentences.zh: 」道盛注《古文尚書》，行於世。

translations.literal: " Daosheng annotated the 《Ancient Text Book of Documents》, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: " Daosheng had annotated the 《Ancient Text Book of Documents》, which circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 真道、方明並坐破仇池，斷割金銀諸雜寶貨，又藏難當善馬，下獄死。

translations.literal: Zhendao and Fangming were both convicted for the defeat of Chouci, having carved off gold, silver, and various treasures, and also concealing Dandang's fine horses; they were cast into prison and died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhendao and Fangming were both convicted for embezzling gold, silver, and other spoils from the conquest of Chouci and for hiding Dandang's fine horses; they were imprisoned and died.

sentences.zh: 劉康祖等繫免各有差。

translations.literal: Liu Kangzu and the others were detained and dismissed, each to a different degree.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kangzu and the others were detained and dismissed to varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 方明，河東人，為劉道濟振武中兵參軍，立功蜀土，歷潁川、南平昌太守，皆坐贓私免官。

translations.literal: Fangming was a man of Hedong; he served as Zhenwu Central Army Staff Officer under Liu Daoji, won merit in the lands of Shu, and successively held the posts of Administrator of Yingchuan and Nanpingchang; in each case he was dismissed for corruption.
translations.idiomatic: Fangming, a native of Hedong, had served as Zhenwu central army staff officer under Liu Daoji, won merit in Shu, and held the prefectures of Yingchuan and Nanpingchang in turn, but was dismissed from each for corruption.

sentences.zh: 孟懷玉，平昌安丘人也。

translations.literal: Meng Huaiyu was a man of Anqiu in Pingchang.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Huaiyu was a native of Anqiu in Pingchang.

sentences.zh: 高祖珩，晉河南尹。

translations.literal: The Gaozu's father Heng was Jin Administrator of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu's father Heng had been Jin administrator of Henan.

sentences.zh: 祖淵，右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yuan was Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yuan was right grand master for splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 父綽，義旗後為給事中，光祿勳，追贈金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His father Chuo, after the righteous banner was raised, became Palace Attendant and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and was posthumously given Grand Master for the Palace with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chuo, after the founding uprising, became palace attendant and grand master for splendid happiness, and was posthumously made grand master for the palace with golden seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 世居京口。

translations.literal: For generations they dwelt at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: The family had long lived at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 高祖東伐孫恩，以懷玉為建武司馬。

translations.literal: When the Gaozu campaigned east against Sun En, he made Huaiyu Jianwu Major.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu campaigned east against Sun En, he made Huaiyu major of the Jianwu command.

sentences.zh: 豫義旗，從平京城，進定京邑。

translations.literal: He took part in the righteous banner, followed in pacifying Jingcheng, and advanced to secure the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the founding uprising, helped pacify Jingcheng, and advanced to secure the capital.

sentences.zh: 以功封鄱陽縣侯，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: For merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Poyang County with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Poyang with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 高祖鎮京口，以懷玉為鎮軍參軍、下邳太守。

translations.literal: When the Gaozu garrisoned Jingkou, he made Huaiyu Garrison Army Staff Officer and Administrator of Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu garrisoned Jingkou, he made Huaiyu staff officer on the garrison army and administrator of Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 義熙三年，出為寧朔將軍、西陽太守、新蔡內史，除中書侍郎，轉輔國將軍，領丹陽府兵，戍石頭。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yixi he went out as Ningshuo General, Administrator of Xiyang, and Interior Governor of Xincai; he was appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat, transferred to General Who Assists the State, took charge of Danyang commandery troops, and garrisoned Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: In Yixi 3 he was sent out as Ningshuo general, administrator of Xiyang, and interior governor of Xincai; he was appointed gentleman of the secretariat, transferred to general who assists the state, given command of Danyang troops, and posted to Shitou.

sentences.zh: 盧循逼京邑，懷玉於石頭岸連戰有功，為中軍諮議參軍。

translations.literal: When Lu Xun pressed the capital region, Huaiyu fought repeatedly at the Shitou shore with merit and was made Central Army Staff Adviser.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Xun threatened the capital, Huaiyu fought repeatedly at Shitou with distinction and was made central army staff adviser.

sentences.zh: 賊帥徐道覆屢欲以精銳登岸，畏懷玉不敢上。

translations.literal: The bandit leader Xu Daofu repeatedly wished to land elite troops on the shore, but feared Huaiyu and did not dare go ashore.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel leader Xu Daofu repeatedly tried to land elite troops on the shore but feared Huaiyu and did not dare come ashore.

sentences.zh: 及循南走，懷玉與眾軍追躡，直至嶺表。

translations.literal: When Xun fled south, Huaiyu and the various armies pursued in his tracks as far as the Lingnan frontier.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun fled south, Huaiyu and the other armies pursued him all the way to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 徐道覆屯結始興，懷玉攻圍之，身當矢石，旬月乃陷。

translations.literal: Xu Daofu massed his forces at Shixing; Huaiyu besieged him, himself facing arrows and stones; after a month and more it fell.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Daofu held Shixing; Huaiyu besieged him, exposing himself to arrow and stone fire; after more than a month the city fell.

sentences.zh: 仍南追循，循平，又封陽豐縣男，食邑二百五十戶。

translations.literal: He then pursued Xun southward; when Xun was pacified, he was again enfeoffed as Baron of Yangfeng County with a fief of two hundred fifty households.
translations.idiomatic: He continued south in pursuit of Xun; when Xun was subdued, he was further enfeoffed as baron of Yangfeng with a fief of two hundred fifty households.

sentences.zh: 復為太尉諮議參軍，征虜將軍。

translations.literal: He again became Grand Marshal Staff Adviser and General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He again became grand marshal staff adviser and general who campaigns against the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 八年，遷江州刺史，尋督江州、豫州之西陽、新蔡、汝南、潁川、司州之弘農、揚州之松滋六郡諸軍事、南中郎將，刺史如故。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to Inspector of Jiangzhou; soon he was put in overall command of military affairs in the six commanderies—Xiyang and Xincai of Yuzhou, Runan and Yingchuan, Hongnong of Sizhou, and Songzi of Yangzhou—and made General of the Southern Gentlemen of the Household; his inspectorate remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was transferred to inspector of Jiangzhou; soon he was given overall command of military affairs in six commanderies—Xiyang and Xincai in Yuzhou, Runan and Yingchuan, Hongnong in Sizhou, and Songzi in Yangzhou—and made general of the southern gentlemen of the household, retaining his inspectorship.

sentences.zh: 時荊州刺史司馬休之居上流，有異志，故授懷玉此任以防之。

translations.literal: At that time Jingzhou Inspector Sima Xiuzhi held the upper reaches and harbored divergent intent; therefore Huaiyu was given this post to guard against him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Jingzhou inspector Sima Xiuzhi held the upper Yangtze and harbored ambitions of his own, so Huaiyu was given the post to keep watch on him.

sentences.zh: 十一年，加持節。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he was granted the staff of authority.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was invested with the staff of command.

sentences.zh: 丁父艱，懷玉有孝性。

translations.literal: He encountered his father's bereavement; Huaiyu had a filial nature.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, Huaiyu showed himself deeply filial by nature.

sentences.zh: 因抱篤疾，上表陳解，不許。

translations.literal: Because he took on a grave illness, he submitted a memorial stating his request to resign; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He then fell seriously ill and submitted a memorial asking to be relieved of office, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 又自陳弟仙客出繼，喪主唯己，乃見聽。

translations.literal: Again he stated himself that his younger brother Xianke had gone out to be adopted as heir elsewhere, and he alone was the chief mourner; only then was he permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He further explained that his brother Xianke had been given in adoption to another line, leaving him solely responsible for the mourning rites, and only then was his resignation approved.

sentences.zh: 未去任，其年卒官。

translations.literal: Before he left his post, in that same year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could leave his post, he died in office that same year.

sentences.zh: 時年三十一。

translations.literal: He was then thirty-one years of age.
translations.idiomatic: He was thirty-one years old at the time.

sentences.zh: 追贈平南將軍。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was enfeoffed with the title General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as general who pacifies the south.

sentences.zh: 子元卒，無子，國除。

translations.literal: His son Yuan died, without sons; the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuan died without heirs, and the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 懷玉別封陽豐男，子慧熙嗣，坐廢祭祀奪爵。

translations.literal: Huaiyu had a separate enfeoffment as Baron of Yangfeng; his son Huixi succeeded; for the offense of neglecting sacrificial rites his rank was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyu also held a separate title as baron of Yangfeng; his son Huixi succeeded him but lost the rank for abandoning the prescribed sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 慧熙子宗嗣，竟陵太守，中大夫。

translations.literal: Huixi's son Zong succeeded; he was Administrator of Jingling and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Huixi's son Zong succeeded him and served as administrator of Jingling and palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 龍符，懷玉弟也。

translations.literal: Longfu was Huaiyu's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Longfu was the younger brother of Meng Huaiyu.

sentences.zh: 驍果有膽氣，幹力絕人。

translations.literal: Bold and resolute, he had daring and spirit; his strength and energy surpassed other men.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce and resolute, he was bold beyond measure and possessed strength that few could match.

sentences.zh: 少好游俠，結客於閭里。

translations.literal: In youth he loved roaming knights-errant and gathered clients in the lanes and hamlets.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he took to the swagger of the knight-errant and gathered followers in his neighborhood.

sentences.zh: 早為高祖所知，既克京城，以龍符為建武參軍。

translations.literal: Early he was recognized by the Gaozu; once the capital region was taken, Longfu was made Jianwu Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu noticed him early on; after the capital was taken, he appointed Longfu staff officer on the Jianwu command.

sentences.zh: 江乘、羅落、覆舟三戰，竝有功。

translations.literal: At the three battles of Jiangcheng, Luoluo, and Fuzhou, he together had merit in all.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself at all three battles—Jiangcheng, Luoluo, and Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 參鎮軍軍事，封平昌縣五等子，加寧遠將軍、淮陵太守。

translations.literal: He participated in Army-of-the-Garrison military affairs, was enfeoffed as fifth-rank Viscount of Pingchang County, and was additionally made General Who Pacifies the Distant and Administrator of Huailing.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the garrison army staff, was enfeoffed as fifth-rank viscount of Pingchang, and further promoted to general who pacifies the distant and administrator of Huailing.

sentences.zh: 與劉藩、向彌征桓歆、桓石康，破斬之。

translations.literal: With Liu Fan and Xiang Mi he campaigned against Huan Xin and Huan Shikang, defeated them, and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: With Liu Fan and Xiang Mi he campaigned against Huan Xin and Huan Shikang, defeating and executing both.

sentences.zh: 除建威將軍、東海太守。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed general who establishes might and administrator of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 索虜斛蘭、索度真侵邊，彭、沛騷擾，高祖遣龍符、建威將軍道憐北討，一戰破之。

translations.literal: The barbarians Hulan and Suduzhen of the Northern Wei invaded the frontier; Peng and Pei were thrown into turmoil; the Gaozu sent Longfu and Jianwei General Daolian north to punish them, and in one battle broke them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Northern Wei generals Hulan and Suduzhen raided the border and threw Peng and Pei into turmoil, Emperor Wu sent Longfu and Jianwei general Liu Daolian north against them; they routed the invaders in a single battle.

sentences.zh: 追斛蘭至光水溝邊，被創奔走。

translations.literal: Pursuing Hulan to the banks of the Guangshui Ditch, they wounded him and he fled.
translations.idiomatic: They pursued Hulan to the Guangshui Ditch, where he was wounded and fled.

sentences.zh: 高祖伐廣固，以龍符為車騎參軍，加龍驤將軍、廣川太守，統步騎為前鋒。

translations.literal: When the Gaozu attacked Guanggu, he made Longfu Chariots-and-Cavalry Staff Officer, additionally General Who is Like a Dragon and Administrator of Guangchuan, commanding infantry and cavalry as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu marched on Guanggu, he made Longfu staff officer on the chariots-and-cavalry command, promoted him to dragon-rising general and administrator of Guangchuan, and put him at the head of the infantry and cavalry vanguard.

sentences.zh: 軍達臨朐，與賊爭水，龍符單騎衝突，應手破散，即據水源，賊遂退走。

translations.literal: The army reached Linqu and contested the water with the bandits; Longfu alone on horseback charged and broke them at once, immediately seized the water source, and the bandits then withdrew in flight.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Linqu and fought the enemy for control of the water, Longfu charged alone on horseback, scattering them at the first blow, seized the springhead, and drove the rebels to retreat.

sentences.zh: 龍符乘勝奔逐，後騎不及，賊數千騎圍繞攻之。

translations.literal: Longfu, riding the victory, pursued in flight; the mounted troops behind could not keep up; several thousand mounted bandits encircled and attacked him.
translations.idiomatic: Longfu pressed the pursuit in the heat of victory, outrunning his escort, until several thousand enemy horsemen surrounded and attacked him.

sentences.zh: 龍符奮矟接戰，每一合輒殺數人，眾寡不敵，遂見害，時年三十三。

translations.literal: Longfu flourished his spear and joined battle; at each encounter he killed several men; numbers few against many could not prevail, and he was slain; he was then thirty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Longfu fought on with leveled spear, killing several men at every pass, but overwhelming numbers prevailed and he fell; he was thirty-three years old.

sentences.zh: 高祖深加痛悼，追贈青州刺史。

translations.literal: The Gaozu deeply mourned and grieved; posthumously he was enfeoffed with the post of Inspector of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu mourned him deeply and posthumously honored him as inspector of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 又表曰：「故龍驤將軍、廣川太守孟龍符，忠勇果毅，隕身王事，宜蒙甄表，以顯貞節，聖恩嘉悼，寵贈方州。

translations.literal: He also memorialized, saying: "The late Dragon-Rising General and Administrator of Guangchuan Meng Longfu was loyal, brave, resolute, and firm; he perished in the king's service. He should receive selection and commendation to display steadfast integrity. Sacred grace has honored him in mourning and favored him with enfeoffment to a territorial inspectorate.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a memorial that said, "The late dragon-rising general and administrator of Guangchuan, Meng Longfu, was loyal, brave, and resolute; he gave his life in the service of the throne. His steadfast devotion deserves public recognition, and your sacred grace has already honored his memory with a posthumous provincial appointment.

sentences.zh: 龍符投袂義初，前驅效命，推鋒三捷，每為眾先。

translations.literal: Longfu, at the raising of righteous arms at the beginning, served as vanguard giving his life, pushed the spear point to three victories, and each time was ahead of the host.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous cause first took up arms, Longfu thrust himself forward as vanguard, won three spearpoint victories, and always led the host.

sentences.zh: 及西劋桓歆，北殄索虜，朝議爵賞，未及施行。

translations.literal: When in the west he executed Huan Xin and in the north exterminated the Northern Wei barbarians, the court deliberated titles and rewards but had not yet carried them out.
translations.idiomatic: After his western campaign against Huan Xin and his northern victories over the barbarians, the court had resolved on rewards but not yet granted them.

sentences.zh: 會今北伐，復統前旅，臨朐之戰，氣冠三軍。

translations.literal: Meeting with the present northern expedition, again he commanded the former brigade; at the battle of Linqu, his spirit crowned the three armies.
translations.idiomatic: On this northern expedition he again led the vanguard; at Linqu his fighting spirit surpassed the whole army.

sentences.zh: 于時逆徒寔繁，控弦掩澤，龍符匹馬電躍，所向摧靡，奪戈深入，知死弗吝。

translations.literal: At that time the rebel host was truly numerous, bowstrings covered the marsh; Longfu on a single horse leapt like lightning; wherever he went he broke and scattered them; seizing spears he plunged deep, knowing death and not sparing himself.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel ranks were thick, archers blackened the marshes, yet Longfu charged alone like lightning, crushing all before him, plunging deep among the enemy spears without sparing his life.

sentences.zh: 賊超奔遁，依險鳥聚，大軍因勢，方軌長驅。

translations.literal: The bandits in panic fled; relying on defile positions they gathered like birds; the great army followed the momentum, aligned their tracks and drove far.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy broke and fled, clustering in defensible strongpoints like frightened birds, while the main army pressed the advantage in a broad advance.

sentences.zh: 考其庸績，豫參濟不，竊謂宜班爵土，以褒勳烈。

translations.literal: Examining his common achievements, he had a share in bringing deliverance; I privately deem it fitting to distribute rank and territory to praise his meritorious exploits.
translations.idiomatic: Weighing his service to the cause, including his role in our victories, I submit that enfeoffment would be the fitting tribute to his merit.

sentences.zh: 」乃追封臨沅縣男，食邑五百戶。

translations.literal: " Thereupon posthumously he was enfeoffed as Baron of Linyuan County with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he was posthumously enfeoffed as baron of Linyuan with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 無子，弟仙客以子微生嗣封。

translations.literal: Having no sons, his younger brother Xianke had his son Weisheng succeed to the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: He had no sons; his brother Xianke's son Weisheng inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 太祖元嘉中，有罪奪爵，徙廣州，以微生弟彥祖子佛護襲爵。

translations.literal: In the Yuankai era of the Taizu, for an offense his rank was stripped and he was banished to Guangzhou; Weisheng's younger brother Yanzu's son Fohu succeeded to the rank.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Wen's Yuankai reign, Weisheng was stripped of his title for a crime and exiled to Guangzhou; Fohu, son of Weisheng's brother Yanzu, inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，國除。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi dynasty took the throne, the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 孝武大明初，諸流徒者悉聽還本，微生已死，子係祖歸京都，有筋幹異力，能儋負數人，入隸羽林，為殿中將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daming under Emperor Xiaowu, all banished and exiled persons were permitted to return to their origins; Weisheng had already died; his son Xizu returned to the capital; he had sinew and frame of unusual strength and could shoulder-load several men; he entered and was enrolled in the Feathered Forest guard and became Palace Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xiaowu's Daming era, all exiles were permitted to return home; Weisheng was already dead, but his son Xizu came back to the capital. Possessed of extraordinary strength, he could carry several men on his back; he enlisted in the Feathered Forest guard and was made palace guard general.

sentences.zh: 二年，索虜寇青、冀，世祖遣軍援之，係祖自占求行。

translations.literal: In the second year, the Northern Wei barbarians raided Qing and Ji; the Shizu sent armies to aid them; Xizu volunteered himself requesting to go.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, barbarians raided Qing and Ji; Emperor Xiaowu sent relief forces, and Xizu volunteered for the campaign.

sentences.zh: 戰於杜梁，挺身入陳，所殺狼籍，遂見殺。

translations.literal: Fighting at Duliang, he bared his body and entered the battle formation; those he killed lay strewn in disorder; he was then killed.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Duliang he plunged into the enemy ranks and killed many, but fell in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 詔書追贈潁川郡太守。

translations.literal: An imperial edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Administrator of Yingchuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict posthumously honored him as administrator of Yingchuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 劉敬宣，字萬壽，彭城人，漢楚元王交後也。

translations.literal: Liu Jingxuan, styled Wanshou, was a man of Pengcheng and a descendant of Prince Yuan of Chu, Jiao, of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jingxuan, courtesy name Wanshou, was a native of Pengcheng and a descendant of Liu Jiao, Prince Yuan of Chu of the Han dynasty.

sentences.zh: 祖建，征虜將軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jian was General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jian served as general who campaigns against the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 父牢之，鎮北將軍。

translations.literal: His father Laozhi was General Who Guards the North.
translations.idiomatic: His father Laozhi was general who guards the north.

sentences.zh: 敬宣八歲喪母，晝夜號泣，中表異之。

translations.literal: Jingxuan at eight years lost his mother; day and night he wailed and wept; his kin within and cousins without found him extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan lost his mother at eight and wept day and night; relatives near and far marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 輔國將軍桓序鎮蕪湖，牢之參序軍事。

translations.literal: General Who Assists the State Huan Xu garrisoned Wuhu; Laozhi participated in Xu's military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When general who assists the state Huan Xu garrisoned Wuhu, Laozhi served on his staff.

sentences.zh: 四月八日，敬宣見眾人灌佛，乃下頭上金鏡以為母灌，因悲泣不自勝，序歎息，謂牢之曰：「卿此兒既為家之孝子，必為國之忠臣。

translations.literal: On the eighth day of the fourth month, Jingxuan saw the multitude bathing the Buddha; he then removed from his head a golden mirror to bathe it for his mother; thereby he wept with grief beyond control; Xu sighed and said to Laozhi: "This son of yours is already a filial son in the family; he is sure to become a loyal minister of the state.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth day of the fourth month, Jingxuan watched others bathe the Buddha image; he took the golden mirror from his head and used it to bathe the statue for his mother's sake, weeping until he could no longer contain his grief. Xu sighed and said to Laozhi, "A son who mourns his mother so deeply at home will surely prove a loyal servant of the state.

sentences.zh: 」起家為王恭前軍參軍，又參會稽世子元顯征虜軍事。

translations.literal: " Beginning his career, he became Vanguard Army Staff Officer under Wang Gong; he also participated in the Campaign-Against-Barbarians military affairs of the Heir of Kuaiji, Yuanxian.
translations.idiomatic: " He entered official life as staff officer on Wang Gong's vanguard command and later joined the staff of Yuan Xian, heir of Kuaiji, on his campaign staff.

sentences.zh: 隆安三年，王恭起兵於京口，以誅司馬尚之兄弟為名。

translations.literal: In the third year of Long'an, Wang Gong raised troops at Jingkou, under the banner of executing the brothers Sima Shangzhi.
translations.idiomatic: In Long'an 3, Wang Gong raised an army at Jingkou on the pretext of punishing the brothers Sima Shangzhi.

sentences.zh: 牢之時為恭前軍司馬、輔國將軍、晉陵太守，置佐領兵。

translations.literal: Laozhi was then Gong's Vanguard Major, General Who Assists the State, and Administrator of Jinling, setting aides and leading troops.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi then served as Wang Gong's vanguard major, general who assists the state, and administrator of Jinling, with staff and troops under his command.

sentences.zh: 而恭以豪戚自居，甚相陵忽，牢之心不能平。

translations.literal: Yet Gong, placing himself as a powerful kinsman, greatly looked down on and slighted him; Laozhi's heart could not be at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Gong treated himself as a grand kinsman of the throne and looked down on Laozhi; Laozhi's resentment grew.

sentences.zh: 及恭此舉，使牢之為前鋒。

translations.literal: When Gong made this move, he made Laozhi his vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When Gong launched his rebellion, he put Laozhi at the head of his army.

sentences.zh: 太傅會稽王道子與牢之書，備言禍福，使以兵反恭。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Prince of Kuaiji Sima Daozi wrote to Laozhi, setting forth fortune and ruin in full, and ordered him to turn his troops against Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Sima Daozi, prince of Kuaiji, wrote to Laozhi in detail about the consequences and urged him to turn his troops against Gong.

sentences.zh: 牢之呼敬宣謂曰：「王恭昔蒙先帝殊恩，今居伯舅之重，義心未彰，唯兵是縱。

translations.literal: Laozhi summoned Jingxuan and said: "Wang Gong in the past received extraordinary grace from the late emperor; now he holds the weighty status of imperial maternal uncle; his righteous intent has not yet been revealed, yet he alone indulges in military force.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi called Jingxuan and said, "Wang Gong once enjoyed exceptional favor from the late emperor and now holds the rank of the emperor's maternal uncle. He has shown no loyal intent, yet unleashes his armies at will.

sentences.zh: 吾不能審恭事捷之日，必能奉戴天子，緝穆宰相與不。

translations.literal: I cannot discern whether, on the day Gong's affair succeeds, he will surely be able to support and uphold the Son of Heaven and harmonize with the chief ministers or not.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot tell whether, if Gong succeeds, he will truly uphold the emperor and work in harmony with the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 今欲奉國威靈，以明逆順，汝以為何如？

translations.literal: Now I wish to uphold the state's august authority to make clear what is rebellious and what is compliant— what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: I mean to uphold the authority of the state and make the line between loyalty and rebellion clear. What do you think?

sentences.zh: 」敬宣曰：「朝廷雖無成、康之隆，未有桓、靈之亂，而恭怙亂阻兵，志陵京邑。

translations.literal: " Jingxuan said: "Though the court lacks the flourishing of Cheng and Kang, it has not yet the disorder of Huan and Ling; yet Gong relies on disorder and obstructs with arms, his intent pressing upon the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: " Jingxuan replied, "The court may not enjoy the golden age of Kings Cheng and Kang, but neither has it sunk to the chaos of Emperors Huan and Ling. Yet Gong takes chaos as his shield and blocks the roads with troops, his ambition set on the capital.

sentences.zh: 大人與恭親無骨肉，分非君臣，雖共事少時，意好不協。

translations.literal: You, my lord, with Gong share no flesh-and-blood kin; your status is not that of lord and minister; though you served together a short time, your minds were not in accord.
translations.idiomatic: You and Gong are not blood kin, nor are you bound as lord and minister. You served together only briefly, and your feelings were never close.

sentences.zh: 今日討之，於情何有？

translations.literal: To attack him today— where is the offense in feeling?
translations.idiomatic: To move against him now would violate no bond of loyalty or kinship.

sentences.zh: 」牢之至竹里，斬恭大將顏延，遣敬宣率高雅之等還京襲恭。

translations.literal: " Laozhi reached Zhuli, beheaded Gong's great general Yan Yan, and sent Jingxuan leading Gao Yazhi and others back to the capital to surprise Gong.
translations.idiomatic: " Laozhi advanced to Zhuli, executed Wang Gong's chief general Yan Yan, and sent Jingxuan with Gao Yazhi and others back to the capital to strike at Gong.

sentences.zh: 恭方出城耀軍，馳騎橫擊之，一時散潰。

translations.literal: Gong had just gone out of the city to display his army; cavalry galloped and struck across them; in a moment they scattered and collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Gong had just led his troops out to parade them when Jingxuan's horsemen charged across their ranks and routed them on the spot.

sentences.zh: 元顯進號後將軍，以敬宣為諮議參軍，加寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: Yuanxian advanced in title to Rear General; Jingxuan was made Staff Adviser and additionally Ningshuo General.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xian was promoted to rear general; Jingxuan was made staff adviser and further promoted to ningshuo general.

sentences.zh: 三年，孫恩為亂，東土騷擾，牢之自表東討，軍次虎疁。

translations.literal: In the third year, Sun En made rebellion; the eastern lands were thrown into turmoil; Laozhi volunteered himself to campaign east; the army halted at Huyao.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Sun En rebelled and threw the east into turmoil; Laozhi volunteered to campaign east and encamped at Huyao.

sentences.zh: 賊皆死戰，敬宣請以騎傍南山趣其後，吳賊畏馬，又懼首尾受敵，遂大敗。

translations.literal: The bandits all fought to the death; Jingxuan requested to take cavalry along the southern mountain to strike their rear; the Wu bandits feared horses and also feared attack front and rear; thereby they suffered great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fought to the death; Jingxuan proposed taking cavalry around the southern hills to hit their rear. The Wu rebels feared cavalry and dreaded being caught between two forces, and were routed.

sentences.zh: 進平會稽，尋加臨淮太守，遷後軍從事中郎。

translations.literal: Advancing, he pacified Kuaiji; soon he was additionally made Administrator of Linhuai and transferred to Rear Army Attending Courtier.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to pacify Kuaiji, was soon made administrator of Linhuai, and was transferred to rear army attending courtier.

sentences.zh: 五年，孫恩又入浹口，高祖戍句章，賊頻攻不能拔。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Sun En again entered Jiekou; the Gaozu garrisoned Gouzhang; the bandits repeatedly attacked but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Sun En invaded Jiekou again; Emperor Wu held Gouzhang, which the rebels assaulted repeatedly without success.

sentences.zh: 敬宣請往為援，賊恩於是退遠入海。

translations.literal: Jingxuan requested to go as relief; the bandit En thereupon withdrew far and entered the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan offered to march to his aid; Sun En then withdrew far out to sea.

sentences.zh: 是時四方雲擾，朝廷微弱，敬宣每慮艱難未已，高祖既累破妖賊，功名日盛，故敬宣深相憑結，情好甚隆。

translations.literal: At this time turmoil clouded the four directions; the court was weak; Jingxuan each time worried that hardship would not end; the Gaozu had repeatedly broken the demonic bandits and his fame and achievement daily flourished; therefore Jingxuan deeply leaned upon and bound himself to him; affection and friendship were very grand.
translations.idiomatic: Turmoil engulfed the realm and the court grew weak; Jingxuan feared the troubles would never end. Emperor Wu, having repeatedly defeated the rebels, rose in fame and power day by day, and Jingxuan placed his trust in him; the two became very close.

sentences.zh: 元顯進號驃騎，敬宣仍隨府轉，軍、郡如故。

translations.literal: Yuanxian advanced in title to Cavalry-in-Chief; Jingxuan still followed the headquarters in transfer; his military and commandery posts remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Xian was promoted to cavalry-in-chief, Jingxuan transferred with his staff; his military and territorial posts remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 元顯驕淫縱肆，群下化之；

translations.literal: Yuanxian was arrogant, licentious, and unrestrained; those beneath him were transformed by him;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xian grew arrogant, dissolute, and unrestrained, and his subordinates followed his example;

sentences.zh: 敬宣每預燕會，未嘗飲酒，調戲之來，無所酬答，元顯甚不說。

translations.literal: Jingxuan each time attended feasts and gatherings, yet never drank wine; when banter and teasing came, he had nothing to reply; Yuanxian was greatly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan attended their banquets but never drank; when teased he offered no response, and Yuan Xian took strong offense.

sentences.zh: 尋進號輔國將軍，餘如故。

translations.literal: Soon he advanced in title to General Who Assists the State; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was promoted to general who assists the state; his other posts were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 元興元年，牢之南討桓玄，元顯為征討大都督，日夜昏酣，牢之驟詣門，不得相見；

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanxing, Laozhi campaigned south against Huan Xuan; Yuanxian was Grand Commander for the Punitive Expedition; day and night he drank in drunken stupor; Laozhi suddenly went to his gate and could not obtain a meeting;
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanxing 1, Laozhi marched south against Huan Xuan; Yuan Xian served as grand commander of the punitive expedition but spent his days and nights in drunken revelry; Laozhi rushed to his gate and could not obtain an audience;

sentences.zh: 帝出餞行，方遇公坐而已。

translations.literal: The emperor came out to bid farewell to the expedition; he only happened to meet him at public session, that was all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came out only to bid the army farewell, and Laozhi met Yuan Xian briefly in formal session and nothing more.

sentences.zh: 桓玄既至溧州，遣信說牢之；

translations.literal: Huan Xuan, having reached Lizhou, sent a messenger to persuade Laozhi;
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan reached Lizhou, he sent envoys to win over Laozhi;

sentences.zh: 牢之以道子昏闇，元顯淫凶，慮平玄之日，亂政方始，假手於玄，誅除執政，然後乘玄之隙，可以得志於天下，將許玄降。

translations.literal: Laozhi, because Daozi was dim and dark and Yuanxian was lewd and vicious, worried that on the day Xuan was pacified disorder in government would just begin; borrowing Xuan's hand, he would eliminate the ruling faction, and then by taking advantage of Xuan's gap he could realize his ambition under heaven; he was about to agree to submit to Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi saw that Daozi was corrupt and Yuan Xian vicious, and reasoned that even if Xuan were defeated, misrule would only worsen. He planned to use Xuan to destroy the ruling clique, then exploit Xuan's weaknesses to seize power himself, and was ready to surrender to him.

sentences.zh: 敬宣諫曰：「方今國家亂擾，四海鼎沸，天下之重，在大人與玄。

translations.literal: Jingxuan remonstrated, saying: "Just now the state is in disorder and turmoil; the four seas boil like a cauldron; the weight of all under Heaven lies with you, my lord, and with Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan urged caution: "The realm is in chaos and the empire seethes; the fate of the land now rests with you and Huan Xuan.

sentences.zh: 玄藉先父之基，據荊南之勢，雖無姬文之德，實為參分之形。

translations.literal: Xuan, relying on his late father's foundation, holds the momentum of southern Jing; though he lacks the virtue of King Wen of Zhou, in truth he has the form of tripartite division.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan builds on his father's power base and holds the strength of southern Jing; he may lack the virtue of King Wen of Zhou, but he already commands a third of the empire.

sentences.zh: 一朝縱之，使陵朝廷，威望既成，則難圖也。

translations.literal: If in one morning you release him and allow him to press upon the court, once his prestige and authority are established, then he will be hard to plot against.
translations.idiomatic: If you let him go now and allow him to overwhelm the court, his authority will solidify and he will become impossible to overthrow.

sentences.zh: 董卓之變，將生於今。

translations.literal: The transformation of Dong Zhuo will be born today.
translations.idiomatic: Another Dong Zhuo will arise from this very moment.

sentences.zh: 」牢之怒曰：「吾豈不知今日取玄如反覆手，但平玄之後，令我那驃騎何？

translations.literal: " Laozhi angrily said: "Do I not know that today taking Xuan is like turning the hand over? But after Xuan is pacified, what am I to do about that Cavalry-in-Chief?
translations.idiomatic: " Laozhi snapped, "Do you think I don't know I could crush Xuan as easily as turning my hand? But once Xuan is gone, what am I to do about that cavalry-in-chief?

sentences.zh: 」遺敬宣為任，玄板為其府諮議參軍。

translations.literal: " He sent Jingxuan as his envoy; Xuan posted him as Staff Adviser on his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent Jingxuan as his envoy, and Xuan appointed him staff adviser on his staff.

sentences.zh: 玄既得志，害元顯，廢道子，以牢之為征東將軍、會稽太守。

translations.literal: Xuan, once his ambition was realized, killed Yuanxian, deposed Daozi, and made Laozhi General Who Campaigns East and Administrator of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xuan secured power, he killed Yuan Xian and deposed Daozi, appointing Laozhi general who campaigns east and administrator of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 牢之與敬宣謀共襲玄，期以明旦。

translations.literal: Laozhi and Jingxuan plotted together to surprise Xuan, setting the time for the next dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi and Jingxuan plotted a joint strike against Xuan, scheduling it for the following dawn.

sentences.zh: 值爾日大霧，府門晚開，日旰，敬宣不至，牢之謂所謀已泄，率部曲向白洲，欲奔廣陵。

translations.literal: It happened that day there was heavy fog; the headquarters gate opened late; the sun set; Jingxuan did not arrive; Laozhi said the plot had already leaked; leading his personal troops he went toward Baizhou, intending to flee to Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: That morning a thick fog delayed the opening of headquarters; dusk came and Jingxuan still had not appeared; Laozhi feared their plot was exposed, gathered his troops, and headed for Baizhou, intending to flee to Guangling.

sentences.zh: 而敬宣還京口迎家，牢之尋求不得，謂已為玄所擒，乃自縊死。

translations.literal: Yet Jingxuan had returned to Jingkou to fetch his family; Laozhi sought him and could not find him; he said Jingxuan had already been captured by Xuan; thereupon he hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan had gone to Jingkou to fetch his family; unable to find him, Laozhi assumed he had been seized by Xuan and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 敬宣奔喪，哭畢，即渡江就司馬休之、高雅之等，俱奔洛陽，往來長安，各以子弟為質，求救於姚興。

translations.literal: Jingxuan ran to the funeral; when the weeping was finished, he immediately crossed the river to join Sima Xiuzhi, Gao Yazhi, and others; together they fled to Luoyang; they traveled back and forth to Chang'an; each sent sons and younger brothers as hostages; they sought rescue from Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan rushed to his father's funeral; when the rites were done he crossed the river to join Sima Xiuzhi and Gao Yazhi; together they fled to Luoyang, traveled to Chang'an, sent their sons as hostages, and sought aid from Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 興與之符信，令關東募兵，得數千人，復還至彭城間，收聚義故。

translations.literal: Xing gave them tallies of trust; ordered them to recruit troops east of the Pass; they obtained several thousand men; again they returned to the region of Pengcheng and gathered old allies of the cause.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing gave them credentials and orders to raise troops east of the Pass; they mustered several thousand men and returned to the Pengcheng region to rally old comrades.

sentences.zh: 玄遣孫無終討冀州刺史劉軌，軌要敬宣、雅之等共據山陽破之，不克。

translations.literal: Xuan dispatched Sun Wuzhong to punish Ji Province Inspector Liu Gui; Gui invited Jingxuan, Yazhi, and others jointly to hold Shanyang and defeat him; they could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan sent Sun Wuzhong against Ji province inspector Liu Gui; Gui summoned Jingxuan and Yazhi to hold Shanyang and strike at Sun, but they failed.

sentences.zh: 又進昌平澗，戰不利，眾各離散，乃俱奔鮮卑慕容德。

translations.literal: Again advancing to Changpingjian, the battle was unfavorable; the host each scattered; thereupon all fled together to the Xianbei ruler Murong De.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing to Changping Stream, they were defeated and their forces scattered; they all fled together to the Xianbei ruler Murong De.

sentences.zh: 敬宣素曉天文，知必有興復晉室者。

translations.literal: Jingxuan from of old understood astronomy and knew that there must be one who would revive the Jin house.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan had long studied the heavens and knew that someone would restore the Jin dynasty.

sentences.zh: 尋夢丸土服之，既覺，喜曰：「丸者桓也。

translations.literal: Soon he dreamed of swallowing a pellet of earth; when he awoke, he said with joy: "The pellet— that is Huan.
translations.idiomatic: He soon dreamed that he swallowed a ball of earth; waking, he exclaimed with delight, "The ball stands for Huan.

sentences.zh: 桓既吞矣，吾復本土乎！

translations.literal: Huan having been swallowed, shall I not return to my native land!
translations.idiomatic: Once Huan is swallowed, I shall return to my homeland!

sentences.zh: 」乃結青州大姓諸崔、封，並要鮮卑大帥免逵，謀滅德，推休之為主，克日垂發。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he joined with the great clans of Qingzhou, the Cuis and Fongs, and also invited the Xianbei great chieftain Miankui; they plotted to destroy De, set up Xiuzhi as leader, and fixed a day near at hand for the rising.
translations.idiomatic: " He then rallied the great Qingzhou clans of Cui and Feng, enlisted the Xianbei chieftain Miankui, plotted to overthrow Murong De and install Xiuzhi as leader, and set a date for the uprising.

sentences.zh: 時劉軌為德司空，大被委任，雅之又欲要軌。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Gui was De's Minister of Works and was greatly entrusted; Yazhi again wished to invite Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gui then served Murong De as minister of works and enjoyed great trust; Gao Yazhi wanted to win him over as well.

sentences.zh: 敬宣曰：「此公年老，吾觀其有安齊志，必不動，不可告也。

translations.literal: Jingxuan said: "This lord is old; I observe that he has the will to settle in Qi; he is sure not to move; he must not be told.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan said, "That man is old, and I see he has made up his mind to live peacefully in Qi; he will never join us. We must not confide in him.

sentences.zh: 」雅之以為不然，遂告軌，軌果不從。

translations.literal: " Yazhi thought otherwise and thereupon told Gui; Gui as expected did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: " Yazhi disagreed, told Liu Gui anyway, and as Jingxuan had predicted, Liu Gui refused.

sentences.zh: 謀頗泄，相與殺軌而去。

translations.literal: The plot leaked considerably; together they killed Gui and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The plot leaked, and they killed Liu Gui and fled together.

sentences.zh: 至淮、泗間，會高祖平京口，手書召敬宣；

translations.literal: Reaching the region between the Huai and the Si, they met with the Gaozu having pacified Jingkou; he personally wrote summoning Jingxuan;
translations.idiomatic: Between the Huai and Si rivers they learned that Emperor Wu had pacified Jingkou; he sent a personal letter summoning Jingxuan;

sentences.zh: 左右疑其詐，敬宣曰：「吾固知其然矣。

translations.literal: Those at his side suspected it was a deception; Jingxuan said: "I have long known it would be thus.
translations.idiomatic: His companions suspected a trap; Jingxuan said, "I have expected exactly this all along.

sentences.zh: 下邳不誘我也。

translations.literal: Xiapi is not luring me.
translations.idiomatic: This is not a trap set at Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 」即便馳還。

translations.literal: " Immediately he galloped back.
translations.idiomatic: " Immediately he spurred his horse homeward.

sentences.zh: 既至京師，以敬宣為輔國將軍、晉陵太守，襲封武岡縣男。

translations.literal: When he had reached the capital, Jingxuan was made General Who Assists the State and Administrator of Jinling, inheriting enfeoffment as Baron of Wugang County.
translations.idiomatic: Once he reached the capital, Liu Yu appointed Jingxuan general who assists the state and administrator of Jinling, with inherited enfeoffment as baron of Wugang County.

sentences.zh: 是歲，安帝元興三年也。

translations.literal: That year was the third year of Yuanxing of Emperor An.
translations.idiomatic: That year was the third year of the Yuanxing era of Emperor An.

sentences.zh: 桓歆率氐賊楊秋寇歷陽，敬宣與建威將軍諸葛長民大破之。

translations.literal: Huan Xin led the Di bandit Yang Qiu to raid Liyang; Jingxuan together with General Who Establishes Might Zhuge Changmin inflicted a great defeat on them.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xin led the Di rebel Yang Qiu in an attack on Liyang; Jingxuan and General Who Establishes Might Zhuge Changmin routed them decisively.

sentences.zh: 歆單騎走渡淮，斬楊秋於練固而還。

translations.literal: Xin alone on horseback fled, crossed the Huai, beheaded Yang Qiu at Liangu, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Xin fled alone on horseback across the Huai; Jingxuan beheaded Yang Qiu at Liangu and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 遷建威將軍、江州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Establishes Might and Inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general who establishes might and inspector of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 敬宣固辭，言於高祖曰：「仇恥既雪，四海清蕩，所願反身草澤，以終餘年。

translations.literal: Jingxuan firmly declined, saying to the Gaozu: "The feud and shame are already avenged and the four seas are cleared and tranquil; what I wish is to turn back to the marshes and grasslands and end my remaining years there.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan firmly declined, telling Liu Yu, "Our feud is settled and the realm is at peace. All I want is to retire to the wilds and live out my days.

sentences.zh: 恩遇不遣，遂復僶俛，即目所忝，已為優渥。

translations.literal: Favored and not dismissed, I again bow to duty; what I hold at present is already generous beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: Your kindness in not releasing me compels me to bend again to office; the honors I already bear are more than enough.

sentences.zh: 且盤龍、無忌猶未遇寵，賢二弟位任尚卑，一朝先之，必貽朝野之責。

translations.literal: Moreover Panlong and Wuji have yet to receive favor; my two worthy younger brothers still hold low posts — if I were placed ahead of them overnight, it would surely draw reproach from court and countryside alike.
translations.idiomatic: Panlong and Wuji have not yet been richly rewarded, and my two younger brothers still hold modest posts. If I were suddenly advanced before them, court and countryside would surely condemn it.

sentences.zh: 」不許。

translations.literal: " The request was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: " His request was denied.

sentences.zh: 敬宣既至江州，課集軍糧，搜召舟乘，軍戎要用，常有儲擬。

translations.literal: Once Jingxuan had arrived at Jiangzhou, he assessed and gathered military grain, sought out and summoned boats and transport, and kept standing stores of essential war materiel.
translations.idiomatic: After Jingxuan took up his post at Jiangzhou, he levied and stockpiled grain, mustered boats and transport, and maintained reserves of everything the army would need.

sentences.zh: 故囗征諸軍雖失利退據，因之每即振復。

translations.literal: Thus the armies of the former [character missing] expedition, though they suffered defeat and retreated to hold positions, through this each time promptly rallied and recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to his stockpiles, even when the field armies suffered setbacks and fell back to defensive positions, they could quickly regroup and recover.

sentences.zh: 其年，桓玄兄子亮自號江州刺史，寇豫章；

translations.literal: That year, Huan Xuan's elder brother's son Liang styled himself Inspector of Jiangzhou and raided Yuzhang;
translations.idiomatic: That year Huan Xuan's nephew Liang declared himself inspector of Jiangzhou and attacked Yuzhang;

sentences.zh: 亮又遣苻宏寇廬陵，敬宣並討破之。

translations.literal: Liang also sent Fu Hong to raid Luling; Jingxuan defeated them both.
translations.idiomatic: Liang also sent Fu Hong against Luling; Jingxuan defeated both forces.

sentences.zh: 初，劉毅之少也，為敬宣寧朔參軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Liu Yi was young, he served as Ningshuo staff officer under Jingxuan.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Liu Yi had served on Jingxuan's staff as a Ningshuo command aide.

sentences.zh: 時人或以雄傑許之，敬宣曰：「夫非常之才，當別有調度，豈得便謂此君為人豪邪？

translations.literal: People at the time sometimes deemed him a heroic figure; Jingxuan said: "Extraordinary talent ought to show its own measure — how can one straightway call this man a peerless hero?
translations.idiomatic: Some had begun to hail him as a hero of the age. Jingxuan said, "A truly extraordinary man reveals himself in his own way. How can we call this fellow a towering talent?

sentences.zh: 其性外寬而內忌，自伐而尚人，若一旦遭逢，亦當以陵上取禍耳。

translations.literal: His nature is outwardly broad yet inwardly jealous, self-praising yet attentive to others; should he one day meet his moment, he will still bring ruin upon himself through insubordination.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly affable, inwardly jealous; eager for praise yet eager to pull others down. When his hour comes, he will still destroy himself by lording it over his superiors.

sentences.zh: 」毅聞之，深以為恨。

translations.literal: " When Yi heard this, he deeply resented it.
translations.idiomatic: " When Yi heard this, he took a lasting grudge.

sentences.zh: 及在江陵，知敬宣還，乃使人言於高祖曰：「劉敬宣父子，忠國既昧，今又不豫義始。

translations.literal: When he was at Jiangling and learned Jingxuan had returned, he sent someone to say to the Gaozu: "Father and son Liu Jingxuan — their loyalty to the state has long been obscure, and now they did not take part at the outset of the righteous cause.
translations.idiomatic: While holding Jiangling he learned Jingxuan had come back and sent word to Liu Yu: "The Jingxuans' loyalty to the throne has always been doubtful, and they did not join us when the righteous cause began.

sentences.zh: 猛將勞臣，方須敘報，如敬宣之比，宜令在後。

translations.literal: Fierce generals and meritorious ministers still await reward in due order — men like Jingxuan ought to be kept at the rear.
translations.idiomatic: The hard-fighting generals and worn ministers still await their rewards; men like Jingxuan should wait their turn at the back of the line.

sentences.zh: 若使君不忘平生，欲相申起者，論資語事，正可為員外常侍耳。

translations.literal: If my lord does not forget our old acquaintance and wishes to raise him up, speaking of seniority and merit, he could properly receive only supernumerary regular attendant.
translations.idiomatic: If you still wish to do something for an old acquaintance, judging by seniority and service he would deserve nothing more than supernumerary attendant at court.

sentences.zh: 聞已授其郡，實為過優；

translations.literal: I hear he has already been given a commandery — that is in truth excessive favor;
translations.idiomatic: I hear he has already been given a whole commandery — that is far too generous;

sentences.zh: 尋知復為江州，尤所駭惋。

translations.literal: Soon learning he was again made Inspector of Jiangzhou, I was especially appalled and grieved.
translations.idiomatic: and now I learn he has been made inspector of Jiangzhou again — that shocks and grieves me most of all.

sentences.zh: 」敬宣愈不自安。

translations.literal: " Jingxuan grew ever more ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: " Jingxuan became only more anxious.

sentences.zh: 安帝反正，自表解職。

translations.literal: When Emperor An was restored, he submitted a memorial of his own requesting to resign office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor An was restored to the throne, Jingxuan petitioned to resign.

sentences.zh: 於是散徹，賜給宅宇，月給錢三十萬。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was released to private life, granted a residence, and given three hundred thousand cash monthly.
translations.idiomatic: He was retired from active service, given a mansion, and a monthly stipend of three hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 高祖數引與遊宴，恩款周洽，所賜錢帛車馬及器服玩好，莫與比焉。

translations.literal: The Gaozu repeatedly invited him to banquets and outings; kindness and intimacy were complete in every respect; gifts of cash, silks, horses and carriages, utensils, robes, and curios — none could compare with him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu repeatedly invited him to hunts and feasts; the warmth between them was complete. Cash, silk, horses, carriages, furnishings, and fine things — no one received gifts like his.

sentences.zh: 尋除冠軍將軍、宣城內史、襄城太守。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed General Who Conquers Champions, Interior Minister of Xuancheng, and Administrator of Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was made general who conquers champions, interior minister of Xuancheng, and administrator of Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 宣城多山縣，郡舊立屯以供府郡費用，前人多發調工巧，造作器物。
