translations.literal: Xuancheng had many mountainous districts; the commandery had formerly established garrison-colonies to supply prefectural expenses; predecessors often conscripted skilled craftsmen to make objects and utensils.
translations.idiomatic: Xuancheng was a rugged, hilly region. The commandery had long maintained colonies to fund its administration; earlier officials had habitually requisitioned artisans to manufacture luxuries.

sentences.zh: 敬宣到郡，悉罷私屯，唯伐竹木，治府舍而已。

translations.literal: When Jingxuan reached the commandery, he abolished all private colonies, merely felling bamboo and timber to repair the government offices, and nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingxuan arrived he abolished the private colonies entirely, using only cut bamboo and timber to repair the yamen — nothing more.

sentences.zh: 亡叛多首出，遂得三千餘戶。

translations.literal: Many fugitive rebels came forward of their own accord, and he thus gained more than three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Many fugitives voluntarily surrendered, yielding more than three thousand registered households.

sentences.zh: 高祖方大相寵任，欲先令立功。

translations.literal: The Gaozu was at this time greatly favoring and trusting him, and wished first to let him earn merit through achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu was showering him with trust and meant first to give him a chance to distinguish himself in battle.

sentences.zh: 義熙三年，表遣敬宣率眾五千伐蜀。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yixi, he memorialized to dispatch Jingxuan leading five thousand troops to campaign against Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yixi he petitioned the throne to send Jingxuan at the head of five thousand men to conquer Shu.

sentences.zh: 國子博士周祗書諫高祖曰：「自義旗之建，所征無不必克，此可謂天人交助，信順之徵也。

translations.literal: Zhou Zhi, Erudite of the National University, wrote remonstrating to the Gaozu: "Since the righteous banner was raised, every campaign has invariably succeeded — this may be called Heaven and man aiding each other, a sign of faithfulness and compliance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zhi, erudite of the National University, wrote to remonstrate with Liu Yu: "Since you raised the banner of righteousness, every campaign you launched has succeeded — a sign that Heaven and men are working together in trust and accord.

sentences.zh: 今大難已夷，君臣俱泰。

translations.literal: Now great calamity is already pacified; lord and ministers alike are at ease.
translations.idiomatic: The great crisis is past; sovereign and ministers alike enjoy peace.

sentences.zh: 頃五穀轉豐，民無饑苦，劫盜之患，亦為弭息，比誠漸足無事，宜大寧治本。

translations.literal: Recently the five grains have grown ever more abundant; the people know no hunger or distress; the scourge of brigands and robbers has also been quieted — at present it is truly gradually sufficient for peace; one ought to seek great tranquillity and cure the root.
translations.idiomatic: Grain harvests are improving, the people no longer go hungry, and banditry has subsided. The realm is at last turning tranquil; now is the time to cultivate lasting order at home.

sentences.zh: 蜀賊宜平，六合宜一，非為不爾也。

translations.literal: The Shu rebels ought to be pacified and the six directions ought to be one — it is not that this should not be so.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels in Shu ought to be crushed and the empire reunited — no one denies that.

sentences.zh: 古人有言，天時不如地利，地利不如人和。

translations.literal: The ancients have a saying: Heaven's season is not as good as Earth's advantage, and Earth's advantage is not as good as human accord.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said that favorable season counts for less than favorable terrain, and terrain for less than harmony among men.

sentences.zh: 今往伐蜀，萬有餘里，溯流天險，動經時歲。

translations.literal: Now to go campaign against Shu is more than ten thousand li; going upstream through Heaven's natural barriers, the movement alone takes seasons and years.
translations.idiomatic: An expedition against Shu means more than ten thousand li, fighting upstream through natural barriers — the march alone would take a year or more.

sentences.zh: 若此軍直指成都，徑禽譙氏者，復是將帥奮威，一快之舉耳。

translations.literal: If this army pointed straight at Chengdu and directly captured the Qiao clan, that would again be the generals exerting their might — a single gratifying stroke, nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: If the army could strike straight for Chengdu and seize the Qiao clan at one blow, that would be a splendid feat of generalship — but only if it worked.

sentences.zh: 然益士荒殘，野無青草，成都之內，殆無孑遺。

translations.literal: Yet the lands of Yi are wasted and devastated; in the fields there is no green grass; within Chengdu, barely a solitary survivor remains.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yi Province lies wasted and bare; the countryside has not a blade of green grass, and Chengdu itself is nearly emptied of people.

sentences.zh: 計得彼利，與今行軍之費，不足相補也。

translations.literal: Counting the gain to be had there against the expense of the present march, it is insufficient to make up the difference.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever could be gained there would not offset the cost of the march.

sentences.zh: 而今往艱險，雨雪方降，驅三州三吳之人，投之三巴三蜀之土，其中疾病死亡，豈可稱計。

translations.literal: Yet now the going is arduous and perilous; rain and snow are just falling; driving the people of the Three Provinces and Three Wu into the lands of the Three Ba and Three Shu — sickness and death among them, how could they be numbered?
translations.idiomatic: The route is brutal, snow is already falling, and you would drive men from Jiangdong into the wilds of Ba and Shu — sickness and death would be beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 此一疑也。

translations.literal: This is the first doubt.
translations.idiomatic: That is my first concern.

sentences.zh: 賊必不守窮城，將決力戰。

translations.literal: The rebels will surely not hold a desperate city; they will resolve to fight with all their strength.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy will not sit besieged in a doomed city — they will fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 今我往勞困，彼來甚逸。

translations.literal: Now we go exhausted; they come very rested.
translations.idiomatic: We would arrive exhausted; they would meet us fresh.

sentences.zh: 若忽使師行不利，人情波駭，大勢挫衂。

translations.literal: If suddenly the army's advance met misfortune, human hearts would surge in alarm and the great momentum would suffer setback and collapse.
translations.idiomatic: One reverse on the march would panic the troops and break the empire's momentum.

sentences.zh: 此二疑也。

translations.literal: This is the second doubt.
translations.idiomatic: That is my second concern.

sentences.zh: 且千里饋糧，士有饑色。

translations.literal: Moreover, to supply grain over a thousand li — the soldiers show the color of hunger.
translations.idiomatic: As the saying goes, armies that must be fed from a thousand li away arrive with hungry faces.

sentences.zh: 況今溯險萬里，所在無儲。

translations.literal: How much more now, going against peril for ten thousand li, with no stores anywhere along the way.
translations.idiomatic: How much worse when the march is ten thousand li against the current, with no depots anywhere along the route?

sentences.zh: 若連兵不解，運漕不繼，雖韓、白之將，何以成功。

translations.literal: If the armies remain engaged without relief and transport and grain supply do not continue, even generals like Han and Bai — how could they succeed?
translations.idiomatic: If the campaign drags on and supply lines fail, not even a Han Xin or a Bai Qi could bring it off.

sentences.zh: 此三疑也。

translations.literal: This is the third doubt.
translations.idiomatic: That is my third concern.

sentences.zh: 今云可征者皆云：『彼親離眾叛。

translations.literal: Those who now say Shu can be attacked all say: 'Their kin are estranged and the multitude has rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Those who urge the expedition say, 'The Qiao regime is torn by internal strife and deserted by its followers.

sentences.zh: 』愚謂不然。

translations.literal: ' I foolishly deem it not so.
translations.idiomatic: ' I do not believe it.

sentences.zh: 彼以一匹夫，而能致今日之事，若眾力離散，亦何以至此。

translations.literal: That man, a lone commoner, was able to bring about today's situation — if the collective strength had scattered, how could he have reached this point?
translations.idiomatic: A single adventurer brought them this far; if his followers were truly falling away, how would he have gotten here?

sentences.zh: 官所遣兵皆烏合受募之人，亦必無千人一心，有前無退矣。

translations.literal: The soldiers the government sends are all a motley assembly of hired recruits — they surely cannot have a thousand hearts as one, advancing without retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Our own troops are hired rabble; they will not march as one man with no thought of retreat.

sentences.zh: 為治者固先定其內而理其外，先安其近而懷其遠。

translations.literal: One who governs ought first to secure the inner and then order the outer, first to settle what is near and then embrace what is far.
translations.idiomatic: Sound governance secures the interior before venturing abroad, stabilizes what is near before dreaming of what is far.

sentences.zh: 自頃狂狡不息，誅戮相繼，未可謂人和也。

translations.literal: Recently crazed and cunning troubles have not ceased; executions and slaughters have followed one upon another — one cannot say there is human accord.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellions and executions have not ceased — one can hardly speak of harmony among men.

sentences.zh: 天險如彼，未可謂地利也。

translations.literal: Natural barriers such as those — one cannot call it Earth's advantage.
translations.idiomatic: With natural barriers like those ahead, one can hardly speak of terrain in our favor.

sentences.zh: 毛脩之家仇不雪，不應以得死為恨；

translations.literal: Mao Xiuzhi's family's feud remains unavenged — he ought not to resent not obtaining death;
translations.idiomatic: Mao Xiuzhi's family blood-debt is still unpaid — we should not simply send him to die satisfied;

sentences.zh: 劉敬宣蒙生存之恩，亦宜性命仰報。

translations.literal: Liu Jingxuan received the grace of having his life spared — he too ought to repay with his very life.
translations.idiomatic: and Liu Jingxuan owes his life to you — he should repay that debt with service, not with suicide.

sentences.zh: 今將軍欲驅二死之甘心，而忘國家之重計，愚情竊所未安。

translations.literal: Now the general wishes to drive these two men who are willing to die, yet forget the weighty reckoning of the state — in my foolish sentiment I privately am not at ease.
translations.idiomatic: To send these two men eager for death while neglecting the nation's larger interests — forgive me, but that troubles me deeply.

sentences.zh: 闕門之外，非所宜豫，苟其有心，不覺披盡。

translations.literal: Beyond the palace gates is not where I ought to intrude; if there is any sincerity in me, I have laid bare everything without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: It is not my place to speak beyond the gate, but I have held nothing back.

sentences.zh: 」不從。

translations.literal: " The Gaozu did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Yu did not accept the advice.

sentences.zh: 假敬宣節，監征蜀諸軍事，郡如故。

translations.literal: Jingxuan was given credentials and made supervisor of all armies campaigning against Shu; his commandery post remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan was given commissary credentials and overall command of the Shu expedition; his commandery post remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 既入峽，分遣振武將軍、巴東太守溫祚以二千人揚聲外水，自率益州刺史鮑陋、輔國將軍文處茂、龍驤將軍時延祖由墊江而進。

translations.literal: Having entered the gorges, he separately dispatched General Who Rouses Martial Might, Administrator of Badong Wen Zuo with two thousand men to make a demonstration on the outer water, while he himself led Inspector of Yizhou Bao Lou, General Who Assists the State Wen Chumao, and General Who is Like a Dragon Shi Yanzu to advance by way of Dianjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Once inside the gorges he sent General Who Rouses Martial Might Wen Zuo, administrator of Badong, with two thousand men to feint along the outer river, while he led Inspector of Yizhou Bao Lou, General Who Assists the State Wen Chumao, and General Who Is Like a Dragon Shi Yanzu up the inner route through Dianjiang.

sentences.zh: 敬宣率先士卒，轉戰而前，達遂寧郡之黃虎，去成都五百里。

translations.literal: Jingxuan took the lead ahead of the soldiers, fighting turn by turn as he advanced, reaching Huanghu in Suining Commandery, five hundred li from Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan fought at the head of his men, battle after battle, until he reached Huanghu in Suining Commandery — five hundred li from Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 偽輔國將軍譙道福等悉眾距險，相持六十餘日，大小十餘戰，賊固守不敢出。

translations.literal: The false General Who Assists the State Qiao Daofu and others brought their full forces to hold the perilous ground; they stalemate for more than sixty days, with more than ten engagements large and small; the rebels held firm and dared not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel general Qiao Daofu massed his troops on the defiles. For more than sixty days they skirmished in a dozen fights, but the enemy held their lines and would not come out.

sentences.zh: 敬宣不得進，食糧盡，軍中多疾疫，死者太半，引軍還。

translations.literal: Jingxuan could not advance; food and grain were exhausted; in the army there was much pestilence; more than half died — he led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan could not break through. Provisions ran out, plague swept the camp, and more than half his men died; he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 譙縱送毛璩一門諸喪，其妻女、文處茂母何，并諸士人喪柩，浮之中流，敬宣皆拯接致歸。

translations.literal: Qiao Zong sent down the coffins of Mao Qiong's entire household and clan, his wife and daughters, Wen Chumao's mother He, together with the coffins of various scholars, floating them midstream; Jingxuan rescued and received them all and sent them home.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zong floated downriver the coffins of Mao Qiong's entire household, his wife and daughters, Wen Chumao's mother Lady He, and several gentry — Jingxuan recovered every coffin and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 為有司所奏，免官，削封三分之一。

translations.literal: Cited by the relevant offices, he was dismissed from office and one third of his fief was cut away.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities impeached him; he was stripped of office and lost one third of his fief.

sentences.zh: 五年，高祖伐鮮卑，除中軍諮議參軍，加冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when the Gaozu campaigned against the Xianbei, Jingxuan was made Central Army Staff Adviser and additionally General Who Conquers Champions.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, when Liu Yu marched against the Xianbei, Jingxuan was made central-army staff adviser with the additional rank of general who conquers champions.

sentences.zh: 從至臨朐，慕容超出軍距戰，敬宣與兗州刺史劉藩等奮擊，大破之。

translations.literal: He followed to Linqu; Murong Chao led his army out to block and fight; Jingxuan with Inspector of Yanzhou Liu Fan and others struck fiercely and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the campaign to Linqu. When Murong Chao marched out to meet them, Jingxuan and Inspector of Yanzhou Liu Fan led a furious charge and routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 龍驤將軍孟龍符戰沒，敬宣并領其眾，圍廣固，屢獻規略。

translations.literal: General Who is Like a Dragon Meng Longfu died in battle; Jingxuan also took command of his forces, besieged Guanggu, and repeatedly offered strategic plans.
translations.idiomatic: When General Who Is Like a Dragon Meng Longfu fell in battle, Jingxuan took over his command, helped besiege Guanggu, and repeatedly offered sound counsel.

sentences.zh: 盧循逼京師，敬宣分領鮮卑虎班突騎，置陣甚整，循等望而畏之。

translations.literal: Lu Xun pressed the capital; Jingxuan separately commanded Xianbei tiger-guard shock cavalry, arraying his lines very orderly; Xun and the others looked upon them and feared them.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Xun threatened the capital, Jingxuan commanded a corps of Xianbei tiger-guard shock cavalry in impeccably drawn ranks — Lu Xun's men looked on in fear.

sentences.zh: 遷使持節、督馬頭、淮西諸軍郡事、鎮蠻護軍、淮南、安豐二郡太守、梁國內史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to bearer of the staff, supervisor of military and commandery affairs for Matou and west of the Huai, General Who Guards the Barbarians, Administrator of the two commanderies Huainan and Anfeng, Interior Minister of Liang, with his generalship unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to bearer of the staff, supervisor of Matou and the Huai west, general who guards the barbarians, administrator of Huainan and Anfeng commanderies, and interior minister of Liang — while retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 循既走，仍從高祖南討，轉左衛將軍，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When Xun had fled, he still followed the Gaozu south in the pursuit, was transferred to Left Guard General, and additionally made Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After Lu Xun fled, he followed Liu Yu south in pursuit, was made left guard general, and received the additional title of regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 敬宣寬厚善待士，多伎藝，弓馬音律，無事不善。

translations.literal: Jingxuan was generous and treated scholars well; he had many skills — archery, horsemanship, music, and harmony — in nothing was he not adept.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan was broad-minded and gracious to men of talent. He mastered archery, horsemanship, music, and a dozen other arts besides.

sentences.zh: 時尚書僕射謝混自負才地，少所交納，與敬宣相遇，便盡禮著歡。

translations.literal: At the time Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Xie Hun prided himself on talent and stature, and seldom formed connections; meeting Jingxuan, he immediately observed full courtesy and displayed warm friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Hun, vice director of the Masters of Writing, was proud of his gifts and station and rarely deigned to befriend anyone — yet when he met Jingxuan he treated him with full ceremony and obvious delight.

sentences.zh: 或問混曰：「卿未嘗輕交於人，而傾蓋於萬壽，何也？

translations.literal: Someone asked Hun: "You have never lightly befriended others, yet under a tilted canopy you warm to Wanshou — why?
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked Hun, "You never make friends lightly, yet you took to Wanshou under a shared cart awning — why?

sentences.zh: 」混曰：「人之相知，豈可以一塗限。

translations.literal: " Hun said: "How men come to know one another — how can this be confined to one path?
translations.idiomatic: " Hun replied, "Friendship does not follow one rule for everyone.

sentences.zh: 孔文舉禮太史子義，夫豈有非之者邪！」

translations.literal: Kong Wenju honored Taishi Ziyi — was there anyone who faulted him for it!"
translations.idiomatic: Kong Wenju honored Taishi Ziyi — who would call that wrong?"

sentences.zh: 初，敬宣回師於蜀，劉毅欲以重法繩之；

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Jingxuan returned his army from Shu, Liu Yi wished to punish him with severe law;
translations.idiomatic: After Jingxuan withdrew from Shu, Liu Yi wanted to have him punished under the harshest laws;

sentences.zh: 高祖既相任待，又何無忌明言於毅，謂不宜以私憾傷至公，若必文致為戮，己當入朝以廷議決之。

translations.literal: the Gaozu having already greatly trusted and favored him, He Wuji also spoke plainly to Yi, saying it was not fitting to let private resentment harm the supreme public good; if charges must be fabricated to execute him, he himself would enter court and let the court assembly decide.
translations.idiomatic: but Liu Yu continued to favor him. He Wuji told Yi plainly that private spite must not override the public good — and that if Yi insisted on framing Jingxuan for execution, he would enter court himself and let the full assembly decide.

sentences.zh: 毅雖止，猶謂高祖曰：「夫生平之舊，豈可孤信。

translations.literal: Yi though he stopped, still said to the Gaozu: "An old friend of a lifetime — how can one trust him alone?
translations.idiomatic: Yi relented, but told Liu Yu, "A lifelong confidant is not someone you can trust blindly.

sentences.zh: 光武悔之於龐萌，曹公失之於孟卓，公宜深慮之。

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwu regretted it with Pang Meng; Duke Cao lost out with Meng Zhuo — my lord ought to ponder this deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu repented his trust in Pang Meng; Cao Cao paid for trusting Zhang Miao. You would do well to think on that.

sentences.zh: 」毅出為荊州，謂敬宣曰：「吾忝西任，欲屈卿為長史、南蠻，豈有見輔意乎？

translations.literal: " Yi went out as Inspector of Jingzhou and said to Jingxuan: "I am unworthily given the western post; I wish to condescend to invite you as Chief Clerk and Director of the Southern Barbarians — is there in you the intent to assist me?
translations.idiomatic: " When Yi took up his post in Jingzhou he said to Jingxuan, "I am honored with the western command and would be pleased to have you as chief clerk and director of the southern barbarians — would you consent to assist me?

sentences.zh: 」敬宣懼禍及，以告高祖。

translations.literal: " Jingxuan feared calamity would reach him and told the Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: " Jingxuan feared a trap and reported it to Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 高祖笑曰：「但令老兄平安，必無過慮。

translations.literal: The Gaozu smiled and said: "Only let elder brother be at peace — there will surely be no excessive worry.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu laughed and said, "So long as your old friend keeps the peace, you need not worry.

sentences.zh: 」出為使持節、督北青州軍郡事、征虜將軍、北青州刺史，領青河太守，尋領冀州刺史。

translations.literal: " He was sent out as bearer of the staff, supervisor of military and commandery affairs of Northern Qingzhou, General Who Punishes the Barbarians, Inspector of Northern Qingzhou, holding the post of Administrator of Qinghe, and soon additionally Inspector of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: " Jingxuan was posted out as bearer of the staff, supervisor of northern Qingzhou, general who punishes the barbarians, and inspector of northern Qingzhou, with concurrent appointment as administrator of Qinghe; soon afterward he also held Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 時高祖西討劉毅，豫州刺史諸葛長民監太尉軍事，貽敬宣書曰：「盤龍狼戾專恣，自取夷滅，異端將盡，世路方夷，富貴之事，相與共之。

translations.literal: At the time the Gaozu was campaigning west against Liu Yi; Inspector of Yuzhou Zhuge Changmin supervised the Grand Marshal's military affairs and sent Jingxuan a letter saying: "Panlong was savage, arrogant, and willful, bringing extinction upon himself; strange and deviant forces are nearly exhausted, the world's path is now becoming level — let us share the matter of wealth and honor together.
translations.idiomatic: While Liu Yu marched west against Liu Yi, Inspector of Yuzhou Zhuge Changmin, acting grand marshal, wrote to Jingxuan: "Panlong's brutal arrogance destroyed him; the last rebels are nearly gone and the age is settling into peace — let us share the rewards together.

sentences.zh: 」敬宣報曰：「下官自義熙以來，首尾十載，遂忝三州七郡。

translations.literal: " Jingxuan replied: "Your humble officer from Yixi onward, from first to last ten years, has unworthily received three inspectorates and seven commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: " Jingxuan replied, "Since Yixi I have served ten years straight and been given three inspectorates and seven commanderies.

sentences.zh: 今此杖節，常懼福過禍生，實思避盈居損；

translations.literal: Now holding this staff, I constantly fear that fortune excessive brings calamity forth; I truly wish to avoid fullness and dwell in diminution;
translations.idiomatic: This new command terrifies me — good fortune overrun invites disaster; I only want to step back from the peak;

sentences.zh: 富貴之旨，非所敢當。

translations.literal: the intent of wealth and honor — it is not what I dare accept.
translations.idiomatic: a share in wealth and power is not something I dare accept.

sentences.zh: 」遣使呈長民書，高祖謂王誕曰：「阿壽故為不負我也。

translations.literal: " He sent a messenger to present Changmin's letter; the Gaozu said to Wang Dan: "A Shou — as expected — has not failed me.
translations.idiomatic: " He forwarded Changmin's letter to Liu Yu, who told Wang Dan, "A Shou has not let me down.

sentences.zh: 」十一年正月，進號右將軍。

translations.literal: " In the first month of the eleventh year, he advanced in title to Right General.
translations.idiomatic: " In the first month of the eleventh year Jingxuan was promoted to right general.

sentences.zh: 司馬道賜者，晉宗室之賤屬也。

translations.literal: Sima Daoci was a low-born kinsman of the Jin imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Daoci was a minor, low-ranking branch of the Jin imperial house.

sentences.zh: 為敬宣參軍。

translations.literal: He served as Jingxuan's staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: He served on Jingxuan's staff.

sentences.zh: 至高祖西征司馬休之，道賜乃陰結同府辟閭道秀及左右小將王猛子等謀反。

translations.literal: When the Gaozu marched west against Sima Xiuzhi, Daoci secretly joined with his colleague in the same office Pilu Daoxiu and the minor generals at his side Wang Mengzi and others to plot rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu marched west against Sima Xiuzhi, Daoci secretly colluded with his colleague Pilu Daoxiu and the junior officers Wang Mengzi and others to plot rebellion.

sentences.zh: 道賜自號齊王，以道秀為青州刺史，規據廣固，舉兵應休之。

translations.literal: Daoci styled himself King of Qi, made Daoxiu Inspector of Qingzhou, planned to hold Guanggu, and raised troops in support of Xiuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Daoci declared himself King of Qi, appointed Daoxiu inspector of Qingzhou, aimed to seize Guanggu, and rose in arms to support Sima Xiuzhi.

sentences.zh: 敬宣召道秀有所論，因屏人，左右悉出戶，猛子逡巡在後，取敬宣備身刀殺敬宣，時年四十五。

translations.literal: Jingxuan summoned Daoxiu for discussion, dismissed attendants, and all his close aides left the room; Mengzi lingered behind, took Jingxuan's bodyguard sword, and killed him; he was forty-five years old.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan summoned Daoxiu for a private talk and sent everyone out; Mengzi hung back, seized Jingxuan's sidearm, and killed him. He was forty-five.

sentences.zh: 文武佐吏即討道賜、猛子等，皆斬之。

translations.literal: Civil and military aides at once campaigned against Daoci, Mengzi, and the rest, and all were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: His civil and military staff immediately moved against Daoci, Mengzi, and the others, and executed them all.

sentences.zh: 先是，敬宣未死，嘗夜與僚佐宴集，空中有放一隻芒屩於坐中，墜敬宣食盤上，長三尺五寸，已經人著，耳鼻間並欲壞。

translations.literal: Earlier, before Jingxuan died, he once feasted at night with his staff; from the air a single straw sandal was cast into the gathering, falling onto Jingxuan's food tray; it was three chi five cun long, already worn by a person, with nose and ears nearly rotted away.
translations.idiomatic: Before his death, Jingxuan once held a night banquet with his officers; a straw sandal dropped from nowhere onto his plate—three feet five inches long, clearly worn, the nose and ears nearly decayed.

sentences.zh: 頃之而敗。

translations.literal: Before long he was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he met his end.

sentences.zh: 喪至，高祖臨哭甚哀。

translations.literal: When the coffin arrived, the Gaozu came in person to mourn and grieved deeply.
translations.idiomatic: When the coffin arrived, Emperor Wu came in person to mourn and wept bitterly.

sentences.zh: 子祖嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zu inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 宋受禪，國除。

translations.literal: When Song received the Mandate, the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liu Song dynasty was founded, the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 檀祗，字恭叔，高平金鄉人，左將軍歆第二弟也。

translations.literal: Tan Zhi, style name Gongshu, was a man of Jinxiang in Gaoping, the second younger brother of Left General Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Zhi, styled Gongshu, was a native of Jinxiang in Gaoping and the second younger brother of Left General Tan Xin.

sentences.zh: 少為孫無終輔國參軍，隨無終東征孫恩，屢有戰功。

translations.literal: In youth he was Fuguo Staff Officer under Sun Wuzhong; following Wuzhong he campaigned east against Sun En and repeatedly won military merit.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he served as staff officer on Sun Wuzhong's staff; campaigning east against Sun En under Wuzhong, he won repeated distinction in battle.

sentences.zh: 復為王誕龍驤參軍。

translations.literal: He again served as Longxiang Staff Officer under Wang Dan.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Longxiang staff officer under Wang Dan.

sentences.zh: 從高祖克京城，參建武軍事。

translations.literal: Following the Gaozu in taking Jingcheng, he joined the Jianwu military staff.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Wu in capturing Jingcheng and joined the Jianwu military staff.

sentences.zh: 至羅落，檀憑之戰沒之後，仍以憑之所領兵配祗。

translations.literal: At Luoluo, after Tan Pingzhi fell in battle, Pingzhi's former command was still assigned to Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: At Luoluo, after Tan Pingzhi was killed in battle, his troops were given to Zhi.

sentences.zh: 京邑既平，參鎮軍事，加振武將軍，隸振武大將軍道規追討桓玄，每戰克捷。

translations.literal: After the capital region was pacified, he joined the garrison army staff, was made Zhenwu General, and under Zhenwu Grand General Daogui pursued and attacked Huan Xuan, winning every battle.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was pacified, he joined the garrison army staff, was made Zhenwu general, and under Zhenwu grand general Liu Daogui pursued Huan Xuan, winning every engagement.

sentences.zh: 江陵平定，道規遣祗征溳、沔亡命桓道兒、張靖、苻嗣等，皆悉平之。

translations.literal: When Jiangling was pacified, Daogui sent Zhi to campaign against the fugitives Huan Dao'er, Zhang Jing, Fu Si, and others of Yun and Mian, and all were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling was secure, Daogui sent Zhi against the fugitives Huan Dao'er, Zhang Jing, Fu Si, and others along the Yun and Mian rivers, and pacified them all.

sentences.zh: 除龍驤將軍、秦郡太守、北陳留內史；

translations.literal: He was appointed Longxiang General, Administrator of Qin Commandery, and Interior Governor of Northern Chenliu;
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Longxiang general, administrator of Qin commandery, and interior governor of Northern Chenliu;

sentences.zh: 又為寧朔將軍、竟陵太守，不拜。

translations.literal: he was also made Ningshuo General and Administrator of Jingling, but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: and was offered the posts of Ningshuo general and administrator of Jingling, but declined.

sentences.zh: 破桓亮於長沙，苻宏於湘東。

translations.literal: He defeated Huan Liang at Changsha and Fu Hong in Xiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated Huan Liang at Changsha and Fu Hong in eastern Xiang.

sentences.zh: 武陵內史庾悅疾病，道規以祗代悅，加寧朔將軍，封西昌縣侯，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: Interior Governor of Wuling Yu Yue fell ill; Daogui had Zhi replace Yue, added Ningshuo General, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Xichang County with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When interior governor of Wuling Yu Yue fell ill, Daogui replaced him with Zhi, promoted him to Ningshuo general, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Xichang with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 五年，入為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he entered the capital as Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was recalled to the capital as gentleman of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 盧循逼京邑，加輔國將軍，領兵屯西明門外。

translations.literal: When Lu Xun pressed the capital region, he was made General Who Assists the State and led troops to garrison outside Ximing Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Xun threatened the capital, he was made general who assists the state and posted with troops outside Ximing Gate.

sentences.zh: 循退走，祗率所領，步道援江陵，未發，遇疾停。

translations.literal: When Xun withdrew, Zhi led his command by land route to relieve Jiangling; before he set out he fell ill and halted.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun withdrew, Zhi led his men overland to relieve Jiangling, but fell ill before he could depart and had to stop.

sentences.zh: 八年，遷右衛將軍，出為輔國將軍、宣城內史，即本號督江北、淮南軍郡事、青州刺史、廣陵相。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to Right Guards General, went out as General Who Assists the State and Interior Governor of Xuancheng, and with his original title oversaw military affairs in Jiangbei and Huainan, became Inspector of Qingzhou, and Chancellor of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was made right guards general, then sent out as general who assists the state and interior governor of Xuancheng, with his existing rank put in charge of Jiangbei and Huainan military affairs, made inspector of Qingzhou, and chancellor of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 進號征虜將軍，加節。

translations.literal: His title was advanced to General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians, with staff of authority added.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general who campaigns against the barbarians and given the staff of authority.

sentences.zh: 十年，亡命司馬國璠兄弟自北徐州界聚眾數百，潛得過淮，因天夜陰暗，率百許人緣廣陵城得入，叫喚直上聽事。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the fugitive brothers Sima Guofan and the rest gathered several hundred men from the border of Northern Xuzhou, secretly crossed the Huai, and taking advantage of a dark night led about a hundred men along the wall of Guangling to enter, shouting as they rushed straight to the main hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the fugitive brothers Sima Guofan and others raised several hundred men on the Northern Xuzhou border, slipped across the Huai, and on a dark night led about a hundred men over the Guangling wall, shouting as they stormed the main hall.

sentences.zh: 祗驚起，出門將處分，賊射之，傷股，乃入。

translations.literal: Zhi started up in alarm, went out the door to take command, and the bandits shot him, wounding his thigh; he then went back inside.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi leaped up, went out to take command, was shot in the thigh, and retreated inside.

sentences.zh: 祗語左右：「賊乘暗得入，欲掩我不備。

translations.literal: Zhi told his attendants: "The bandits used the darkness to enter and mean to catch me unprepared.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi told his men, "The rebels used the dark to slip in and hoped to catch us off guard.

sentences.zh: 但打五鼓，懼曉，必走矣。

translations.literal: Just beat the fifth watch drum; fearing dawn, they are sure to flee."
translations.idiomatic: Beat the fifth watch drum. Once they fear dawn is near, they will surely run."

sentences.zh: 」賊聞鼓鳴，謂為曉，於是奔散，追討殺百餘人。

translations.literal: " Hearing the drums, the bandits thought it was dawn and scattered in flight; pursuing them, more than a hundred were killed.
translations.idiomatic: " Hearing the drums, the rebels thought day had broken and fled; a pursuit killed more than a hundred.

sentences.zh: 祗降號建武將軍。

translations.literal: Zhi was reduced in rank to Jianwu General.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was demoted to Jianwu general.

sentences.zh: 十一年，進號右將軍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year his title was advanced to Right General.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was promoted to right general.

sentences.zh: 十二年，高祖北伐，而亡命司馬囗寇涂

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, as the Gaozu marched north, a fugitive Sima [character missing] raided Tu
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, while Emperor Wu marched north, a fugitive Sima [name missing] raided Tu

sentences.zh: 〈涂或作滁〉

translations.literal: 〈Tu is also written Chu〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Tu is also written Chu〉

sentences.zh: 中，秦郡太守劉基求救，分軍掩討，即破斬之。

translations.literal: zhong; Administrator of Qin Commandery Liu Ji sought relief; Zhi sent detached troops in surprise attack and at once defeated and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: prefecture; Qin commandery administrator Liu Ji appealed for help; Zhi sent a detachment in surprise attack and at once defeated and killed the rebel.

sentences.zh: 十四年，宋國初建，天子詔曰：「宋國始立，內外草創，禁旅王要，總司須才。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, when the State of Song was first established, the Son of Heaven edicted: "The State of Song has just been founded; within and without all is newly made; the imperial guard and royal duties require men of talent to oversee them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, when the Song state was first established, the emperor edicted, "Song has just been founded; court and realm are still being built; the palace guard and royal household need able men at their head.

sentences.zh: 右將軍祗可為宋領軍將軍，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Right General Zhi may serve as Song's General Who Leads the Army, with added title of Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Right General Zhi shall be Song's general who leads the army, with the added title of cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 」祗性矜豪，樂在外放恣，不願內遷，甚不得志。

translations.literal: " Zhi was proud and overbearing by nature, delighted in unrestrained service abroad, unwilling to move inward, and deeply discontent.
translations.idiomatic: " Proud by nature, Zhi loved the freedom of command in the provinces and hated the capital posting; he was deeply frustrated.

sentences.zh: 發疾不自治，其年卒廣陵，時年五十一。

translations.literal: He fell ill and did not treat himself; that year he died at Guangling, aged fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill and neglected his health; that year he died at Guangling, at the age of fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈散騎常侍、撫軍將軍，諡曰威侯。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and General Who Pacifies the Army; his posthumous title was Marquis Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and general who pacifies the army, with the posthumous title Marquis Wei.

sentences.zh: 子獻嗣，元熙中卒，無子，祗次子朗紹封。

translations.literal: His son Xian succeeded; he died in the Yuanxi era without a son, and Zhi's second son Lang continued the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xian inherited the title; Xian died in the Yuanxi era without an heir, and Zhi's second son Lang succeeded to the fief.

sentences.zh: 朗卒，子宣明嗣。

translations.literal: When Lang died, his son Xuanming succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Lang died, his son Xuanming inherited.

sentences.zh: 宣明卒，子逸嗣。

translations.literal: When Xuanming died, his son Yi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanming died, his son Yi inherited.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，國除。

translations.literal: When Qi received the Mandate, the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi dynasty was founded, the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：劉敬宣與高祖恩結龍潛，義分早合，雖興復之始，事隔逢迎，而深期久要，未之或爽。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Liu Jingxuan and the Gaozu bound their kindness while still in obscurity; their bond of righteousness joined early; although at the beginning of restoration their affairs were separated by formal reception, their deep expectation and long-standing pact were never in the least betrayed.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Liu Jingxuan and Emperor Wu forged their bond while still obscure men; their loyalty to one another was pledged early. Though at the dawn of restoration formal courtesies kept them apart for a time, their deep trust and long alliance never wavered.

sentences.zh: 隆赫之任，義止於人存；

translations.literal: Lofty and brilliant appointments owed their meaning only to the man's survival;
translations.idiomatic: The grandest offices meant nothing once the man was gone;

sentences.zh: 飾終之數，無聞於身後。

translations.literal: the rites due the dead were not heard of after his passing.
translations.idiomatic: and the honors due the dead were never granted after his death.

sentences.zh: 恩禮之有厚薄者，將有以乎！

translations.literal: That favor and ritual should have such uneven measure—must there not be a reason for it!
translations.idiomatic: That favor and ceremony should be meted out so unevenly—surely there was a reason for it!
